events.note: Longespée died on 7 March 1226 at Salisbury Castle. Matthew Paris claimed he was poisoned by Hubert de Burgh, but historians regard the accusation as undoubtedly false. He was buried in Salisbury Cathedral.

deathCause.summary: Died at Salisbury Castle; poison claim discredited
deathCause.detail: William Longespée died on 7 March 1226 at Salisbury Castle. Matthew Paris alleged he was poisoned by Hubert de Burgh, but historians (e.g. Matthew Strickland) regard the accusation as undoubtedly false. He was buried in Salisbury Cathedral.
deathCause.summaryCn: 在索尔兹伯里城堡去世；中毒说已不可信
deathCause.detailCn: 威廉·朗斯佩于1226年3月7日在索尔兹伯里城堡去世。马修·帕里斯声称其被休伯特·德·伯格下毒，但史学家（如马修·斯特里克兰）认为这一指控纯属不实。葬于索尔兹伯里大教堂。

sourceNote: Dates and facts from the English Wikipedia article 'William Longespée, 3rd Earl of Salisbury' (text and infobox), fetched 2026-08-17.
notes: Acknowledged illegitimate son of Henry II and Ida de Tosny, recognised by his father in 1188 with the honour of Appleby. Married Ela of Salisbury (1196) and became Earl of Salisbury. Led the fleet at Damme (1213), commanded the right wing at Bouvines (1214), and stayed loyal to John in 1215 (not a Magna Carta surety). Died 1226. Birth year corrected to c. 1167 per Wikipedia ('in or before 1167'); some older references give c. 1176. Spouse and children are not in the roster, so relationship refs remain empty.

fullNameCn: 摩根·菲茨罗伊

events.label: Provost of Beverley Minster
events.labelCn: 任贝弗利大教堂教长
events.note: The list of provosts of Beverley Minster records Morgan as provost 1212-1217. Raised by his mother Nest's husband Ralph Bloet, he was well treated by his half-brother King John.

events.label: Elected Bishop of Durham; consecration refused by the pope
events.labelCn: 当选达勒姆主教，教皇拒绝祝圣
events.note: Nominated to the see of Durham between 7 March and 7 May 1215. Pope Innocent III refused consecration on the grounds of Morgan's illegitimacy; when offered confirmation if he would deny that Henry II was his father, Morgan refused. The election was quashed.

events.label: Died
events.labelCn: 去世
events.note: The article does not record his death date, place or cause; he is conventionally dated to c. 1217 (he held the provostship of Beverley until 1217).

deathCause.summary: Date and cause of death not recorded
deathCause.detail: Morgan's death is not recorded in the sources: the Wikipedia article gives no date, place or cause. He is conventionally dated to c. 1217, when his provostship of Beverley ended.
deathCause.summaryCn: 死期与死因均未见记载
deathCause.detailCn: 摩根的逝世未见史料记载：维基百科条目未给出日期、地点或死因。通常推定其卒于约1217年，即其贝弗利教长任期结束之时。

sourceNote: Dates and facts from the English Wikipedia article 'Morgan (bishop)', fetched 2026-08-17. NOTE: the previous wikiUrl 'Morgan_(bishop-elect_of_Durham)' returns 404; corrected to the live article.
notes: Illegitimate son of Henry II and Nest (Nesta), daughter of Iorwerth ab Owain of Caerleon; raised by Nest's husband Ralph Bloet. Provost of Beverley (1212-1217), elected Bishop of Durham in 1215 but never consecrated — Pope Innocent III rejected him for illegitimacy, and Morgan refused to deny that Henry II was his father. Record is thin: birth date unknown (presumably late 1180s), death c. 1217. No evidence of the excommunication by John sometimes suggested.

fullNameCn: 行者罗洛
deathPlace: Duchy of Normandy (buried at Rouen Cathedral)
birthPlaceCn: 斯堪的纳维亚（挪威或丹麦；有争议）
deathPlaceCn: 诺曼底公国（葬于鲁昂大教堂）

events.label: Viking raids on West Francia; traditional seizure of Rouen
events.note: Dudo of Saint-Quentin places Rollo taking Rouen in 876; modern scholars dispute this and he may not have reached West Francia until after 876.
events.labelCn: 洗劫西法兰克；传统记载攻取鲁昂

events.label: Took part in the Viking Siege of Paris (885-886)
events.labelCn: 参与维京人对巴黎的围城（885–886 年）

events.label: Siege of Chartres; defeated by the Franks
events.note: The Frankish victory under Robert of France helped bring about the treaty with Charles the Simple.
events.labelCn: 围攻沙特尔，为法兰克人所败

events.label: Treaty of Saint-Clair-sur-Epte; granted Normandy
events.note: The 911 date rests on later tradition (Dudo of Saint-Quentin); the earliest independent evidence is a charter of 918, and some historians date the agreement c. 911-912. Rollo received the lands between the Epte and the sea in exchange for allegiance and baptism.
events.labelCn: 《圣克莱尔-叙尔-埃普特条约》；获授诺曼底

events.label: Baptized at Rouen
events.note: Took the baptismal name Robert after his godfather, Robert I of France. Some scholars argue the conversion was only formal at first and paganism persisted.
events.labelCn: 在鲁昂受洗

events.label: Passed the Norman succession to William Longsword
events.note: Rule passed by c. 927-928; Rollo is last mentioned by the chronicler Flodoard in 928.
events.labelCn: 将诺曼继承权传给长剑威廉

events.label: Death of Rollo
events.note: Died c. 930; sources place his death between his last mention in 928 and 933. Buried at Rouen Cathedral; cause of death unrecorded.
events.labelCn: 罗洛去世

notes: First ruler of Normandy, commonly styled Count of Rouen. Early dates are approximate. Origins debated: Dudo of Saint-Quentin claimed he was Danish, while Icelandic/Norwegian sagas identify him with Hrolfr of More, western Norway. Treaty dating: 911 per later tradition, earliest independent evidence a charter of 918. His rule passed to William Longsword by c. 927-928; he died between 928 and 933.

deathCause.detail: Rollo died c. 930 (sources place his death between his last mention by Flodoard in 928 and 933); the surviving accounts do not establish a reliable cause of death. He was buried at Rouen Cathedral.
deathCause.detailCn: 罗洛约于 930 年去世（史料将其死期定于 928 年最后一次被弗洛多阿尔提及至 933 年之间）；现存史料无法确立可靠的死因。他安葬于鲁昂大教堂。

fullNameCn: 鲁昂伯爵长剑纪尧姆
birthPlaceCn: 诺曼底或英格兰（不确定）
deathPlaceCn: 西法兰克索姆河畔皮基尼

events.label: Succeeded Rollo as Count of Rouen
events.note: Rollo lived on for about five more years; rule passed c. 927-928.
events.labelCn: 继承罗洛成为鲁昂伯爵

events.label: Recognized King Rudolph; granted Cotentin and Avranchin
events.note: In exchange for recognizing Rudolph as king of West Francia, William received lordship over much of the lands of the Bretons, including Avranches, the Cotentin Peninsula and the Channel Islands.
events.labelCn: 承认鲁道夫国王；获授科唐坦与阿夫朗尚

events.label: Birth of his son Richard (the future Richard I)
events.note: Richard was born c. 933 to Sprota, William's more danico (non-Christian) wife.
events.labelCn: 儿子理查（未来的理查一世）出生

events.label: Marriage to Luitgarde of Vermandois
events.note: Daughter of Count Herbert II of Vermandois; the union produced no children.
events.labelCn: 与韦尔芒杜瓦的吕特加德成婚

events.label: Received King Louis IV on his return from England
events.note: William was among the Norman magnates who received the new king of West Francia, called back from exile in England.
events.labelCn: 迎接自英格兰归来的国王路易四世

events.label: Conflict with Arnulf I of Flanders
events.note: William aided his brother-in-law Herluin II of Montreuil against Arnulf; Arnulf retaliated against Normandy, and William was excommunicated for ravaging Arnulf's estates.
events.labelCn: 与佛兰德的阿努尔夫一世交战

events.label: Assassinated by Arnulf's followers at Picquigny
events.note: Ambushed and killed while attending a peace conference on an island in the Somme at Picquigny.
events.labelCn: 在皮基尼遭阿努尔夫党羽刺杀

notes: Second ruler of Normandy; contemporary sources called him Count of Rouen, and 'duke' only came into common usage in the 11th century. Son of Rollo and Poppa of Bayeux. Assassinated on 17 December 942 at Picquigny by followers of Arnulf I of Flanders; his son Richard I (aged about ten) succeeded him. Birth year approximate (c. 893), possibly in England.

deathCause.detail: William Longsword was ambushed and killed on 17 December 942 by followers of Arnulf I of Flanders while attending a peace conference at Picquigny, on an island in the Somme.
deathCause.culprit: Followers of Arnulf I, Count of Flanders
deathCause.detailCn: 942 年 12 月 17 日，长剑纪尧姆在索姆河皮基尼岛与佛兰德伯爵阿努尔夫一世进行和谈时，遭阿努尔夫党羽伏击杀害。
deathCause.culpritCn: 佛兰德伯爵阿努尔夫一世的党羽

fullNameCn: 无畏者理查一世

events.label: Succeeded his murdered father at about age ten
events.note: Richard was about ten when William Longsword was killed on 17 December 942. King Louis IV first installed him, then seized duchy lands and held Richard at Laon until Norman knights (led by Osmond de Centville and Bernard the Dane) secured his release.
events.labelCn: 年仅约十岁继承遭弑之父的领地

events.label: Defeated King Louis IV; recognized as duke
events.note: Allied with Norman and Viking leaders plus men sent by Harald Bluetooth; Louis IV was captured and the subsequent Treaty of Gerberoy (c. 947) recognized Richard as duke.
events.labelCn: 击败路易四世；《热伯鲁瓦条约》承认理查为公爵

events.label: Marriage to Emma of Paris, daughter of Hugh the Great
events.note: Connected Richard directly to the House of Capet; Emma died after March 968 with no issue.
events.labelCn: 与巴黎的埃玛成婚（强者于格之女）

events.label: Repelled the invasion of Theobald I of Blois
events.note: Count Theobald I of Blois invaded in 962 but was routed before crossing the Seine.
events.labelCn: 击退布卢瓦的蒂博一世入侵

events.label: Marriage to Gunnor (more danico); children legitimized
events.note: Gunnor was of Viking/Danish descent; Richard married her to legitimize their children, including the future Richard II. Date not precisely recorded (mid-960s).
events.labelCn: 与古诺尔结合，子女获合法地位

events.label: Alliance with the new King of the Franks, Hugh Capet
events.note: Richard had been made guardian of the young Hugh Capet in 955; his marriage to Emma of Paris tied him to the Capetian house.
events.labelCn: 与法兰克新王于格·卡佩结盟

events.label: Rebuilt Fécamp Abbey
events.note: Richard restored the abbey destroyed by Viking raids; he was later buried there.
events.labelCn: 重建费康修道院

events.label: Death of Richard I
events.note: Died of natural causes at Fécamp; buried at Fécamp Abbey. Succeeded by his son Richard II.
events.labelCn: 理查一世去世

notes: Ducal terminology for early Norman rulers varies by source; this card uses the conventional modern title. Born c. 932-933 (Wikipedia infobox gives 28 August 932 at Fécamp). Succeeded at about age ten after his father's murder. In his last 30 years he made Normandy the most cohesive and formidable principality in West Francia. Died of natural causes on 20 November 996; father of Richard II.

deathCause.detail: Richard I died of natural causes on 20 November 996 at Fécamp, aged about 64, and was buried at Fécamp Abbey.
deathCause.detailCn: 理查一世于 996 年 11 月 20 日在费康自然去世，享年约 64 岁，安葬于费康修道院。

events.label: Marriage to Ealhswith of Mercia
events.labelCn: 与默西亚的艾尔斯威丝结婚
events.note: Ealhswith came from Mercian nobility; the marriage cemented ties with Mercia.

events.label: Battle of Ashdown
events.labelCn: 阿什当战役
events.note: 9 January 871, four days after the Danish victory at Reading; Alfred's forces prevailed.

events.label: Became King of Wessex
events.labelCn: 成为威塞克斯国王
events.note: Succeeded his brother Æthelred I on his death in April 871; reign dated from 23 April 871.

events.label: Danish surprise attack on Chippenham; Alfred retreats to Athelney
events.labelCn: 丹麦军突袭奇彭纳姆，阿尔弗雷德退守阿塞尔内
events.note: Guthrum's forces struck at Chippenham on Twelfth Night (early January 878); Alfred withdrew to the marshes of Athelney.

events.label: Battle of Edington
events.labelCn: 爱丁顿战役
events.note: May 878; Alfred mustered the fyrd in the seventh week after Easter (4–10 May) and decisively defeated Guthrum.

events.label: Treaty of Wedmore; baptism of Guthrum
events.labelCn: 《韦德莫尔条约》与古斯鲁姆受洗
events.note: Guthrum and 29 of his leading men were baptised at Aller, with Alfred as godfather; the formal Treaty of Alfred and Guthrum partitioning the Danelaw followed c. 879–886.

events.label: Captured London
events.labelCn: 攻占伦敦
events.note: Alfred occupied and restored London in 886, placing it under Mercian control.

events.label: Took the title King of the Anglo-Saxons
events.labelCn: 改用「盎格鲁-撒克逊人之王」称号
events.note: From c. 886 Alfred styled himself King of the Anglo-Saxons, signalling overlordship of all English not under Danish rule.

events.label: Issued the law code (Doom Book)
events.labelCn: 颁布律法汇编《末日法典》
events.note: Compiled in the late 880s or early 890s, drawing on earlier codes including those of Æthelberht, Ine and Offa; part of Alfred's broader programme of learning.

events.label: Built a network of fortified burhs
events.labelCn: 营建要塞城镇（布尔赫）防御体系
events.note: Fortified towns were built from the 880s during the peace after Edington; the Burghal Hidage records the system's obligations.

events.label: Repelled renewed Viking invasions (892–896)
events.labelCn: 击退892–896年维京人的再度入侵
events.note: Large Viking fleets invaded from autumn 892/893; the campaign ended when the invaders gave up around 896.

events.label: Battle of Buttington
events.labelCn: 布廷顿战役
events.note: Dated 893 or 894 in different sources; combined West Saxon and Mercian forces defeated a besieged Viking army.

events.label: Death at Winchester
events.labelCn: 于温切斯特去世
events.note: Died 26 October 899; the precise illness is not recorded in contemporary sources.

sourceNote: Birth year debated: Asser gives 849, but West Saxon genealogical evidence implies 847–848; 849 is used here as the mainstream figure. Traditional birthplace Wantage is not independently attested.
notes: Maternal ancestor of Empress Matilda through the royal House of Wessex. Reformer of law and defence: issued a law code, built the burh network, and sponsored a programme of learning (court school and translations).

deathCause.summary: Died of illness in old age (specific illness not recorded)
deathCause.detail: Alfred died at Winchester on 26 October 899 after a long period of declining health; contemporary sources do not identify the precise illness.
deathCause.summaryCn: 老年患病去世（具体病因未载）
deathCause.detailCn: 899 年 10 月 26 日，阿尔弗雷德在长期健康衰退后于温彻斯特去世；当时的史料未能确证具体病因。

fullNameCn: 阿尔弗雷德大帝

primaryTitleCn: 盎格鲁-撒克逊人的国王

titles.title: King of the Anglo-Saxons
titles.titleCn: 盎格鲁-撒克逊人的国王

sourceNote: Son of Alfred the Great; birth year not recorded (historians estimate the mid-870s) and his birth place is unknown, so 'Wessex' is approximate; the exact date of the Battle of Tettenhall (5 August 910) rests on the Anglo-Saxon Chronicle.
notes: King of the Anglo-Saxons 899-924; with his sister Æthelflæd he reconquered the southern Danelaw from the Vikings.

deathCause.detail: Edward died at Farndon-on-Dee, Cheshire, on 17 July 924, shortly after suppressing a revolt by Mercians and Welsh at Chester; no cause of death is recorded. His son Ælfweard may have reigned in Wessex briefly before Æthelstan became king.
deathCause.detailCn: 924 年 7 月 17 日长者爱德华在镇压切斯特的麦西亚人与威尔士人叛乱后不久，卒于柴郡迪河畔法恩登；死因无记载。其子埃尔夫沃德可能在威塞克斯短暂在位，随后埃塞尔斯坦继位。

events.label: Succeeded Alfred as King of the Anglo-Saxons
events.labelCn: 继承阿尔弗雷德成为盎格鲁-撒克逊人的国王
events.note: Alfred died on 26 October 899; Edward was accepted by the West Saxons and Mercians, though his cousin Æthelwold disputed the succession.

events.label: Crowned at Kingston upon Thames
events.labelCn: 于泰晤士河畔金斯顿加冕
events.note: Crowned on 8 June 900 at Kingston upon Thames.

events.label: Battle of the Holme: revolt of Æthelwold ended
events.labelCn: 霍尔姆战役：埃塞尔沃尔德叛乱终结
events.note: Fought on 13 December 902; the Danes won the battle but Æthelwold was killed, ending the threat to Edward's throne.

events.label: Battle of Tettenhall: decisive defeat of the Northumbrian Danes
events.labelCn: 特滕霍尔战役：大败诺森布里亚丹麦人
events.note: A combined Mercian and West Saxon army inflicted a decisive defeat on the Northumbrian Danes; the date of 5 August 910 is from the Anglo-Saxon Chronicle.

events.label: Conquest of the East Anglian Danelaw: Tempsford, Colchester, Maldon
events.labelCn: 征服东盎格利亚丹麦法区：坦普斯福德、科尔切斯特、莫尔登
events.note: The decisive year: English forces stormed Tempsford and killed the last Danish king of East Anglia, took Colchester and relieved Maldon; the Danes of East Anglia, Cambridge and Northampton submitted.

events.label: Took Stamford and Nottingham; imposed direct rule on Mercia
events.labelCn: 夺取斯坦福与诺丁汉，对麦西亚实行直接统治
events.note: Stamford and Nottingham surrendered in 918; after Æthelflæd's death (June 918) her daughter Ælfwynn was deposed in December 918 and Mercia was brought under Edward's direct rule.

events.label: At Bakewell the kings of Scots, Northumbrians and Strathclyde accepted him as overlord
events.labelCn: 贝克韦尔会盟：苏格兰、诺森布里亚与斯特拉斯克莱德诸王承认其宗主权
events.note: At Bakewell in the Peak District the kings of the Scots, Rægnald, the Northumbrians and the Strathclyde Welsh 'chose him as father and lord'; modern historians are sceptical that this was a real submission.

events.label: Died at Farndon-on-Dee, Cheshire
events.labelCn: 卒于柴郡迪河畔法恩登
events.note: 17 July 924; succeeded by Æthelstan, though his son Ælfweard may have been king of Wessex for about a month before his own death in August 924.

fullNameCn: 长者爱德华

sourceNote: Eldest son of Edward the Elder and first king to effectively rule all England; birth year approximate (c. 894), and the 924 vs 925 start of his reign is disputed (Wessex delayed his coronation until 925).
notes: Grandson of Alfred the Great; never married and had no children, succeeded by his half-brother Edmund I.

deathCause.detail: Æthelstan died at Gloucester on 27 October 939, aged about 45; no contemporary source records the cause of death, presumed to have been illness. He was buried at Malmesbury Abbey by his own wish.
deathCause.detailCn: 939 年 10 月 27 日埃塞尔斯坦卒于格洛斯特，享年约 45 岁；当代史料未记载死因，推测为疾病。按其遗愿葬于马尔姆斯伯里修道院。

events.label: Born in Wessex, traditionally at Winchester, c. 894
events.labelCn: 出生于威塞克斯（传统称温彻斯特），约 894 年
events.note: Year approximate, based on William of Malmesbury's claim that he was thirty years old when he came to the throne in 924.

events.label: Accepted as King of the Anglo-Saxons by the Mercians
events.labelCn: 被麦西亚人拥立为盎格鲁-撒克逊人的国王
events.note: The Mercians accepted him on Edward the Elder's death in July 924; opposition in Wessex delayed his coronation until September 925.

events.label: Crowned King of the Anglo-Saxons at Kingston upon Thames
events.labelCn: 于泰晤士河畔金斯顿加冕为盎格鲁-撒克逊人的国王
events.note: Crowned on 4 September 925 by Archbishop Athelm of Canterbury.

events.label: Marriage of his sister to Sihtric, Viking king of York
events.labelCn: 将姐妹嫁给约克维京国王西特里克
events.note: January 926; after Sihtric's death in 927 Æthelstan seized York, completing the conquest.

events.label: Conquest of York and Northumbria
events.labelCn: 征服约克与诺森布里亚
events.note: Seized York after Sihtric's death in 927; Ealdred of Bamburgh was driven out and Northumbria brought under his rule.

events.label: Meeting at Eamont: Scottish and northern kings accept his overlordship
events.labelCn: 埃蒙特会盟：苏格兰与北方诸王承认其宗主权
events.note: 12 July 927; Constantine II of Scotland, Hywel Dda, Ealdred of Bamburgh and Owain of Strathclyde accepted his overlordship.

events.label: Styled King of the English — first king of all England
events.labelCn: 称英格兰人的国王——首位全英格兰之王
events.note: From 927 his charters and coins used grand titles such as Rex totius Britanniae, 'King of the whole of Britain'.

events.label: Half-sister Eadgyth married the future Emperor Otto I
events.labelCn: 异母妹埃德吉斯嫁给未来的皇帝奥托一世
events.note: 929 or 930; Æthelstan sent two half-sisters to the court of Henry the Fowler, and Otto chose Eadgyth as his bride.

events.label: Invaded Scotland; Constantine II acknowledged his overlordship
events.labelCn: 入侵苏格兰，君士坦丁二世承认其宗主权
events.note: Campaign of May 934; by September Constantine witnessed a charter as subregulus.

events.label: Battle of Brunanburh: decisive victory over the Norse-Scottish alliance
events.labelCn: 布鲁南博尔战役：大败诺斯-苏格兰联军
events.note: Autumn 937; exact day unrecorded. An overwhelming victory over the allied Norsemen, Scots and Strathclyde Britons, celebrated in the famous poem in the Anglo-Saxon Chronicle.

events.label: Died at Gloucester
events.labelCn: 卒于格洛斯特
events.note: 27 October 939; buried at Malmesbury Abbey, Wiltshire.

fullNameCn: 英格兰人的国王埃塞尔斯坦

sourceNote: Son of Edward the Elder and king of the English; the chronology of the Northumbrian succession struggles of 947-954 is 'very unclear' and contested by historians.
notes: Youngest son of Edward the Elder and Eadgifu; completed the reduction of Northumbria; close friend of St Dunstan; died unmarried.

deathCause.detail: Eadred died at Frome, Somerset, on 23 November 955 after ill health that worsened in his last years and led to his early death at about 32; contemporaries describe him sucking the juice from food, suggesting a chronic digestive ailment.
deathCause.detailCn: 955 年 11 月 23 日埃德雷德卒于萨默塞特弗罗姆；晚年健康状况不断恶化，终致约 32 岁早逝。时人记载他进食时只吸食汤汁，提示慢性消化系统疾病。

events.label: Succeeded his brother Edmund I as King of the English
events.labelCn: 继承兄长埃德蒙一世成为英格兰人的国王
events.note: Edmund was killed at Pucklechurch on 26 May 946; his sons were young children, so Eadred succeeded.

events.label: Crowned at Kingston upon Thames by Archbishop Oda
events.labelCn: 由坎特伯雷大主教奥达在金斯顿加冕
events.note: Crowned on 16 August 946; in the same year he reduced all Northumbria under his rule and received promises of obedience from the Scots.

events.label: Northumbrian magnates submitted at Tanshelf
events.labelCn: 诺森布里亚权贵在坦谢尔夫归顺
events.note: At Tanshelf, Archbishop Wulfstan and the York magnates pledged allegiance to Eadred.

events.label: Ravaged Northumbria; burned Ripon Minster; ambushed at Castleford
events.labelCn: 蹂躏诺森布里亚，焚毁里彭大教堂，在卡斯尔福德遭伏击
events.note: The York magnates had accepted Erik Bloodaxe as king; Eadred ravaged Northumbria and burned Ripon Minster to punish Wulfstan, then was ambushed on his return at Castleford; the Northumbrians soon deserted Erik and paid compensation.

events.label: Arrested and deposed Archbishop Wulfstan
events.labelCn: 逮捕并废黜大主教伍尔夫斯坦
events.note: In 952 Eadred arrested Wulfstan for his repeated dealings with the Scandinavian kings of York; the archbishop was later released (probably early 955) to the bishopric of Dorchester-on-Thames.

events.label: Final submission of Northumbria; Erik Bloodaxe expelled
events.labelCn: 诺森布里亚最终归顺；血斧埃里克被逐
events.note: In 954 the York magnates threw out Erik Bloodaxe, this time permanently; Erik was assassinated shortly afterwards, and Osulf of Bamburgh was appointed the first ealdorman of all Northumbria.

events.label: Died at Frome after a long illness
events.labelCn: 久病后卒于弗罗姆
events.note: 23 November 955; succeeded by his nephew Eadwig.

fullNameCn: 英格兰人的国王埃德雷德

fullName: Eadgifu of Wessex, Queen of West Francia

events.label: Marriage to Charles the Simple, King of West Francia
events.labelCn: 与西法兰克国王查理三世（天真汉）结婚
events.note: Eadgifu became Charles the Simple's second wife, married between 917 and 919 after the death of his first wife Frederuna; queen consort of West Francia from 919.

events.label: Fled to England with her son Louis after Charles's deposition
events.labelCn: 查理被废后携子路易逃往英格兰
events.note: In 923 Charles the Simple was deposed after the Battle of Soissons and taken prisoner by Count Herbert II of Vermandois; Eadgifu fled with the infant Louis to England, where he was raised at the court of her half-brother Æthelstan.

events.label: Returned to France; her son Louis IV crowned King of West Francia
events.labelCn: 返回法兰西；其子路易四世加冕为西法兰克国王
events.note: In 936 Louis IV was called back from England and crowned king of West Francia, with Eadgifu accompanying him; she then retired to a convent at Laon.

events.label: Abduction by and marriage to Herbert the Old, Count of Omois
events.labelCn: 被奥莫瓦伯爵老赫伯特掳走成婚
events.note: In 951, to her son Louis IV's great anger, Eadgifu was abducted and married by Herbert the Old, Count of Omois; the circumstances are poorly documented.

events.label: Death at Soissons (in or after 951)
events.labelCn: 在苏瓦松去世（951年或其后）
events.note: Eadgifu died at Soissons on 26 December in an unknown year; she is not recorded after 951, so the death is dated 'in or after 951'. The record's death year of 955 is an approximation.

sourceNote: Daughter of Edward the Elder and queen of West Francia. Birth year not recorded; died 'in or after 951' (record value 955); queen consort of West Francia 919–923.
notes: Daughter of Edward the Elder and his second wife Ælfflæd. Married Charles the Simple of West Francia (917–919); fled with her son Louis to England in 923 after Charles was deposed; Louis was raised at the court of her half-brother Æthelstan and became king of West Francia in 936. She retired to Laon and is last recorded in 951. Her husband Charles the Simple and son Louis IV are not in the roster. Note: this Eadgifu is the queen of West Francia — not Eadgifu of Kent, the mother of Edmund I. Birth year is not recorded (record value 902 is an approximation).

deathCause.summary: Died in or after 951 (exact year unknown)
deathCause.detail: Eadgifu died at Soissons on 26 December in an unknown year; she is not recorded after 951, so the mainstream dating is 'in or after 951'. The record's value of 955 is an approximation.
deathCause.summaryCn: 卒于951年或其后（确切年份不详）
deathCause.detailCn: 伊德吉芙在某年12月26日卒于苏瓦松；951年之后史料再无记载，故主流定年为「951年或其后」。记录中的955年为近似值。

fullNameCn: 西法兰克王后伊德吉芙

sourceNote: Daughter of Edward the Elder; identity is distinct from other women of the same name.
notes: Basic card; event timeline intentionally left empty.
fullNameCn: 威塞克斯公主埃尔夫吉芙

fullName: Eadgyth of Wessex, Queen of Germany

events.label: Marriage to Otto (later Otto I, Holy Roman Emperor)
events.labelCn: 与奥托（后来的神圣罗马帝国皇帝奥托一世）结婚
events.note: In 930 Henry the Fowler requested the match and Æthelstan sent Eadgyth and her sister Eadgifu to Germany; Otto chose Eadgyth. Otto had already granted her Magdeburg as dower in 929.

events.label: Became Queen of East Francia/Germany; crowned separately from Otto
events.labelCn: 成为东法兰克（德意志）王后，与奥托分别受膏加冕
events.note: On Otto's accession in 936 Eadgyth became queen of East Francia (Germany), crowned and anointed separately from her husband.

events.label: Co-founded the Monastery of St Maurice at Magdeburg
events.labelCn: 与奥托共建马格德堡圣莫里斯修道院
events.note: In 937 Eadgyth and Otto co-founded the Monastery of St Maurice at Magdeburg, later the site of her burial and of Magdeburg Cathedral.

events.label: Reconciled Otto with his mother
events.labelCn: 促成奥托与其母和解
events.note: In 941 Eadgyth effected a reconciliation between Otto and his mother; she also helped introduce the cult of Saint Oswald of Northumbria into Germany.

events.label: Death at Magdeburg
events.labelCn: 在马格德堡去世
events.note: Eadgyth died at Magdeburg on 26 January 946, aged about 35–36; her death was unexpected. Her remains, identified by isotope analysis in 2010, are the oldest known remains of a member of English royalty.

sourceNote: Daughter of Edward the Elder and queen of Germany. Married Otto in 930; died 26 January 946 at Magdeburg.
notes: Daughter of Edward the Elder and his second wife Ælfflæd; sister of Eadgifu of Wessex. Married Otto, later Emperor Otto I, in 930; queen of East Francia/Germany from 936, crowned separately from Otto. Mother of Liudolf, Duke of Swabia, and Liutgard. This is the Eadgyth who married Otto I — distinct from Edith of Polesworth and Edith of Wilton. Her husband Otto I and children are not in the roster.

deathCause.summary: Died at Magdeburg on 26 January 946; cause not recorded
deathCause.detail: Eadgyth died at Magdeburg on 26 January 946, aged about 35–36; her death was unexpected and the cause is not recorded. She was buried in the monastery of St Maurice, later Magdeburg Cathedral.
deathCause.summaryCn: 946年1月26日卒于马格德堡，死因未载
deathCause.detailCn: 伊德吉丝于946年1月26日在马格德堡去世，年约35–36岁；她的死出乎意料，死因未见记载。她葬于圣莫里斯修道院，即后来的马格德堡大教堂。

fullNameCn: 德意志王后伊德吉丝

deathPlaceCn: 格洛斯特郡帕克尔彻奇

events.label: Became King of the English on Æthelstan's death
events.labelCn: 埃塞尔斯坦去世后继位为英格兰人的国王
events.note: Succeeded his half-brother Æthelstan on 27 October 939; William of Malmesbury implies he was about 18.

events.label: Coronation at Kingston-upon-Thames (Advent Sunday)
events.labelCn: 在泰晤士河畔金斯顿加冕（将临期主日）
events.note: Probably crowned c. 1 December 939 (Advent Sunday), likely at Kingston-upon-Thames.

events.label: Marriage to Ælfgifu of Shaftesbury
events.labelCn: 与沙夫茨伯里的埃尔夫吉芙结婚
events.note: Married probably around the time of his accession; Ælfgifu, mother of his sons Eadwig and Edgar, died in 944 and was venerated as a saint.

events.label: Loss of the Five Boroughs; treaty at Leicester with Olaf Guthfrithson
events.labelCn: 丧失五城地区；与奥拉夫·古斯弗里特松在莱斯特订约
events.note: Anlaf Guthfrithson stormed Tamworth and the treaty mediated by Archbishop Wulfstan of York surrendered the Five Boroughs — the first serious setback for the English since Edward the Elder's reconquest.

events.label: Recovered the Five Boroughs
events.labelCn: 收复五城地区
events.note: In 942 Edmund recovered Lincoln, Leicester, Nottingham, Stamford and Derby, commemorated by a poem in the Anglo-Saxon Chronicle.

events.label: Baptism of Anlaf Sihtricson with Edmund as godfather
events.labelCn: 奥拉夫·西特里克松受洗，埃德蒙任其教父
events.note: The Norse king of York was baptised in 943 with Edmund as godfather, cementing peace.

events.label: Expelled the Viking kings of York
events.labelCn: 驱逐约克的维京国王
events.note: In 944 Edmund expelled the remaining Norse kings of York, regaining control over the whole of England.

events.label: Ravaged Strathclyde; ceded it to Malcolm I of Scotland for a defensive pledge
events.labelCn: 蹂躏斯特拉斯克莱德，为换取防御盟约将其交给苏格兰国王马尔科姆一世
events.note: Edmund ravaged Strathclyde in 945 and handed it to Malcolm I of Scotland in return for a pledge of defensive alliance.

events.label: Killed by an outlaw at Pucklechurch
events.labelCn: 在帕克尔彻奇被亡命之徒杀害
events.note: Killed on 26 May 946 at Pucklechurch, Gloucestershire, while trying to rescue his steward from the outlaw Leofa; a minority view (Downham, Halloran) sees political assassination. Buried at Glastonbury Abbey.

sourceNote: Birth year 920/921 (record value 921); death 26 May 946 at Pucklechurch per the Anglo-Saxon Chronicle tradition as related by John of Worcester.
notes: Son of Edward the Elder and his third wife Eadgifu of Kent; elder brother of King Eadred. Also styled Edmund the Elder, Edmund the Just and Edmund the Magnificent (Edmundus Magnificus). Recovered the Five Boroughs (942), expelled the Viking kings of York (944) and ceded Strathclyde to Malcolm I of Scotland in 945 for a defensive alliance. His mother, his wives (Ælfgifu of Shaftesbury, Æthelflæd of Damerham) and his elder son Eadwig are not in the roster.

deathCause.summary: Killed by an outlaw at Pucklechurch while defending his steward
deathCause.detail: Edmund was killed on 26 May 946 at Pucklechurch, Gloucestershire, while trying to rescue his steward from the outlaw Leofa, who stabbed him to death; the story is recorded in the Anglo-Saxon Chronicle tradition (John of Worcester). A minority scholarly view (Downham, Halloran) argues political assassination, but most historians accept the chronicle account.
deathCause.summaryCn: 在帕克尔彻奇为保护管家而被亡命之徒杀害
deathCause.detailCn: 946年5月26日，埃德蒙在格洛斯特郡帕克尔彻奇为保护管家而与亡命之徒莱奥法（Leofa）搏斗，被其刺杀身亡；此说见于《盎格鲁-撒克逊编年史》传统（约翰·伍斯特转述）。少数学者（唐纳姆、哈洛伦）认为是政治暗杀，但多数史家接受编年史的记载。

fullNameCn: 英格兰人的国王埃德蒙一世

events.label: Became King of Mercia when the kingdom was divided
events.labelCn: 王国分裂后成为默西亚国王
events.note: In 957 the kingdom was divided: Edgar became King of the Mercians (with the Thames as boundary) while his brother Eadwig kept Wessex.

events.label: Became King of all England on Eadwig's death
events.labelCn: 埃德威格去世后继位为全英格兰国王
events.note: On 1 October 959 Edgar became king of all England; coinage was still issued in Eadwig's name until then.

events.label: Dunstan appointed Archbishop of Canterbury
events.labelCn: 邓斯坦出任坎特伯雷大主教
events.note: At the start of Edgar's reign Dunstan, recalled from exile, became Archbishop of Canterbury — a pillar of the Benedictine Reform.

events.label: Marriage to Ælfthryth
events.labelCn: 与埃尔夫特里特结婚
events.note: Edgar married Ælfthryth, widow of Ealdorman Æthelwold, in 964; she was consecrated queen in 973. Her sons were Edmund (d. 971) and Æthelred the Unready.

events.label: Coronation of Edgar and Ælfthryth at Bath (Whit Sunday)
events.labelCn: 在巴思为埃德加与埃尔夫特里特加冕（圣灵降临节）
events.note: 11 May 973, Whit Sunday: Edgar was crowned at Bath, described in the Chronicle as if a first coronation though he had reigned since 959 — historians debate its significance.

events.label: Submission of kings at Chester
events.labelCn: 切斯特诸王臣服
events.note: At Chester in 973 six (ASC D) or eight (Ælfric) kings submitted to or allied with Edgar; the famous story of Edgar being rowed on the River Dee by the kings comes only from 12th-century writers and is traditional, not contemporary.

events.label: Backed the English Benedictine Reform; Regularis Concordia
events.labelCn: 支持英格兰本笃会改革运动，颁布《统一修院规程》
events.note: Edgar strongly supported the monastic reform led by Dunstan, Oswald and Æthelwold; the Regularis Concordia (c. 973) established a single monastic rule.

events.label: Death, aged 31–32; buried at Glastonbury Abbey
events.labelCn: 去世，享年31–32岁，葬于格拉斯顿伯里修道院
events.note: Edgar died on 8 July 975, aged 31 or 32. The Anglo-Saxon Chronicle records no place; Winchester is traditionally given (John of Worcester). His death triggered the succession struggle between Edward the Martyr and Æthelred.

sourceNote: Born 943 or 944 (record value 943; his mother died the year he was born); died 8 July 975. The Chester rowing story is a 12th-century tradition, not contemporary evidence.
notes: Son of Edmund I and his first wife Ælfgifu of Shaftesbury. Nicknamed the Peaceful/Peacemaker because his reign was free of serious external conflict; it was also the high point of the English Benedictine Reform. His consorts (Æthelflæd Eneda, Wulfthryth, Ælfthryth) and sons Edward the Martyr and Edmund (d. 971) are not in the roster.

deathCause.detail: Edgar died on 8 July 975; contemporary sources record no illness and the cause of death is unknown. He was buried at Glastonbury Abbey. The traditional death place Winchester is given by John of Worcester but not by the Anglo-Saxon Chronicle.
deathCause.detailCn: 975年7月8日埃德加去世，当时史料未记载任何病症，死因不明。他葬于格拉斯顿伯里修道院。传统说法其死于温彻斯特出自约翰·伍斯特，编年史未载具体地点。

fullNameCn: 和平者埃德加

events.label: Became king after the murder of his half-brother Edward the Martyr
events.labelCn: 同父异母兄殉道者爱德华遇害后继位
events.note: Edward the Martyr was killed at Corfe on 18 March 978; Æthelred, aged about 9–12, came to the throne in deeply troubled circumstances.

events.label: Consecration at Kingston-upon-Thames
events.labelCn: 在泰晤士河畔金斯顿受膏加冕
events.note: The Anglo-Saxon Chronicle says he was consecrated at Kingston 'with much rejoicing' over a year after his accession; the common dating is Easter 979 (14 April), but the day is uncertain.

events.label: Battle of Maldon; Byrhtnoth killed; first large Danegeld paid
events.labelCn: 莫尔登战役；比尔特诺斯战死；首次缴纳巨额丹麦金
events.note: In August 991 Ealdorman Byrhtnoth was defeated and killed by Vikings at Maldon; England paid 10,000 pounds to make them leave — the first large Danegeld.

events.label: Olaf Tryggvason and Sweyn Forkbeard attacked; tribute paid; Olaf baptised
events.labelCn: 奥拉夫·特里格瓦松与斯韦恩·福克比尔德入侵；纳贡；奥拉夫受洗
events.note: In 994 the Norwegian Olaf Tryggvason and the Dane Sweyn Forkbeard besieged London; England paid 16,000 pounds and Æthelred sponsored Olaf's confirmation, after which Olaf promised never to return in hostility.

events.label: Marriage to Emma of Normandy
events.labelCn: 与诺曼底的埃玛结婚
events.note: In 1002 Æthelred married Emma, sister of Duke Richard II of Normandy — a key dynastic alliance with Normandy; their sons included Edward the Confessor.

events.label: St Brice's Day massacre of Danes
events.labelCn: 圣布赖斯日屠杀丹麦人
events.note: On 13 November 1002 Æthelred ordered the killing of all Danish men in England; the order is known from his charter of 1004 and its scale is debated by historians.

events.label: Sweyn Forkbeard's conquest of England; flight into exile in Normandy
events.labelCn: 斯韦恩·福克比尔德征服英格兰；流亡诺曼底
events.note: From August 1013 Sweyn launched a full conquest; London held out but the country submitted, and by December 1013 Æthelred fled to his wife's family in Normandy.

events.label: Returned from exile after Sweyn's death; restored to the throne
events.labelCn: 斯韦恩死后自流亡地归来复位
events.note: Sweyn died on 3 February 1014; Æthelred returned, received pledges of loyalty from the magnates (the first recorded pact between an English king and his subjects) and drove out Sweyn's son Cnut.

events.label: Cnut's invasion (1015–1016); Eadric Streona's defection; Edmund's rebellion
events.labelCn: 克努特入侵（1015–1016年）；埃德里克·斯特雷奥纳叛变；埃德蒙起兵
events.note: Cnut landed in autumn 1015 and conquered the north; Ealdorman Eadric Streona defected to him, while Æthelred's son Edmund revolted against his father. Æthelred, ill and suspicious, remained in London.

events.label: Death in London during Cnut's siege
events.labelCn: 克努特围攻伦敦期间在伦敦去世
events.note: Æthelred died in London on 23 April 1016 while Cnut besieged the city; he was buried in Old St Paul's Cathedral and was succeeded by his son Edmund Ironside.

sourceNote: Birth c. 966–969 (record value 966); death 23 April 1016 in London. His byname 'Unready' renders Old English unræd, 'ill-advised'.
notes: Son of Edgar the Peaceful and Queen Ælfthryth (daughter of Ordgar, ealdorman of Devon) — a different Ælfthryth from the roster's Ælfthryth, Countess of Flanders, so no link is drawn. His byname 'Unready' (Old English unræd) is a pun meaning 'ill-advised' or 'no counsel', not 'unprepared'. His first wife Ælfgifu of York and second wife Emma of Normandy are not in the roster. Modern scholarship views his reign more sympathetically than the old condemnation: achievements in legislation, coinage and literature stand against the catastrophic end of his reign.

deathCause.summary: Died of illness in London during Cnut's siege
deathCause.detail: Æthelred died in London on 23 April 1016, while Cnut's forces were besieging the city; the Anglo-Saxon Chronicle attributes his death to illness. Some later writers claimed he was murdered or died of grief, but the mainstream view is natural death after a period of sickness.
deathCause.summaryCn: 克努特围攻伦敦期间因病去世
deathCause.detailCn: 1016年4月23日，在克努特围攻伦敦期间，埃塞尔雷德二世在伦敦病逝；《盎格鲁-撒克逊编年史》记载其死于疾病。后世个别记载称其遭谋杀或忧伤而死，但主流观点为自然死亡。

fullNameCn: 决策无方者埃塞尔雷德二世

events.label: Marriage to Ealdgyth, widow of Sigeferth
events.labelCn: 与西格弗斯的遗孀埃尔迪丝结婚
events.note: In 1015 Edmund married Ealdgyth, widow of the murdered thegn Sigeferth, illegally and against his father's will — a direct challenge to Æthelred.

events.label: Became King of the English after Æthelred's death
events.labelCn: 埃塞尔雷德二世去世后继位为英格兰国王
events.note: On 23 April 1016, after his father's death in London, Edmund was chosen king by the Londoners and the witan, continuing the war against Cnut.

events.label: Chosen and probably crowned in London
events.labelCn: 在伦敦被拥立并可能加冕
events.note: Edmund was 'probably crowned' in London in 1016, likely by Archbishop Lyfing of Canterbury; the ceremony is not securely recorded.

events.label: Battle of Penselwood (victory over Cnut)
events.labelCn: 彭塞尔伍德战役（击败克努特）
events.note: In June 1016 Edmund fought Cnut at Penselwood in Somerset; the sources record the engagement as a success for Edmund in the summer campaign.

events.label: Battle of Sherston (indecisive)
events.labelCn: 谢尔斯顿战役（未分胜负）
events.note: In the last week of June 1016 Edmund fought Cnut at Sherston in Wiltshire; the battle was indecisive after two days of fighting.

events.label: Battle of Assandun; decisive defeat by Cnut
events.labelCn: 阿桑顿战役，败于克努特
events.note: On 18 October 1016 Edmund was decisively defeated at Assandun (site uncertain, possibly Ashingdon, Essex); the flight of Eadric Streona was blamed for the rout.

events.label: Treaty of Alney (Olney); England divided with Cnut
events.labelCn: 阿尔内（奥尔尼）条约；与克努特瓜分英格兰
events.note: After Assandun, Edmund and Cnut agreed at Alney near Deerhurst to partition England: Edmund kept Wessex, Cnut took the north — a short-lived division before Edmund's death.

events.label: Death; cause unknown
events.labelCn: 去世，死因不明
events.note: Edmund died on 30 November 1016, possibly at London or Oxford, months into his reign; after his death Cnut took all England. Contemporary sources do not record the cause.

sourceNote: Birth c. 990–993 (record value 988, adjusted to 990 per mainstream scholarship); death 30 November 1016, cause unknown.
notes: Son of Æthelred the Unready and his first wife Ælfgifu of York. Birth year is uncertain: historians place it between 990 and 993; he was possibly born at Æthelingadene (Singleton, West Sussex) and raised by his grandmother Queen Ælfthryth. His byname 'Ironside' appears in sources from c. 1057 and reflects his warrior reputation. His wife Ealdgyth and younger son Edmund Ætheling are not in the roster.

deathCause.summary: Died 30 November 1016, months into his reign; cause unknown
deathCause.detail: Edmund died on 30 November 1016, possibly at London or Oxford, only months after the treaty with Cnut. Contemporary sources do not record the cause: disease, exhaustion from campaigning or battle injuries are all possible. The 11th-century chronicler Adam of Bremen claimed poisoning, and 12th-century writers told of murder, but modern historians regard these as unreliable (possibly folklore).
deathCause.summaryCn: 即位数月后于1016年11月30日去世，死因不明
deathCause.detailCn: 1016年11月30日，埃德蒙在与克努特订约后仅数月即去世，地点可能在伦敦或牛津。当代史料未记载死因：疾病、征战劳累或战伤均有可能。11世纪不莱梅的亚当声称其被毒杀，12世纪文献则记载遇刺，现代史家均认为这些说法不可靠（可能出自民间传说）。

fullNameCn: 铁骨埃德蒙二世

events.label: Exiled with his brother Edmund; sent to the Swedish court of Olof Skötkonung
events.labelCn: 与弟弟埃德蒙一同流亡，被送往瑞典国王奥洛夫·舍特科农的宫廷
events.note: After the Danish conquest, Cnut sent the infant Edward and his brother Edmund to the Swedish court — supposedly to be killed — but Olof Skötkonung, an old ally of their grandfather, refused. The brothers' subsequent fate is poorly documented.

events.label: Raised at the court of King Stephen I of Hungary
events.labelCn: 在匈牙利国王斯蒂芬一世宫廷中长大
events.note: Most reconstructions place Edward's upbringing at the Hungarian court of King Stephen I (c. 1019–1046); some place the brothers instead at the Kievan court of Yaroslav the Wise. The evidence is speculative.

events.label: Marriage to Agatha (origins disputed)
events.labelCn: 与阿加莎结婚（其出身有争议）
events.note: Edward's wife Agatha — mother of Margaret of Scotland, Christina and Edgar the Ætheling — is recorded, but her origins are disputed; the exact year of the marriage is unknown (c. 1035–1045).

events.label: Returned to Hungary with Andrew
events.labelCn: 随安德鲁返回匈牙利
events.note: Edward and his family likely accompanied Andrew (later Andrew I) back to Hungary in 1046 and may have fought with his army; the details are reconstructed from later sources.

events.label: Recalled by Edward the Confessor as heir to the English throne
events.labelCn: 被忏悔者爱德华召回，指定为英格兰王位继承人
events.note: In 1056 Edward the Confessor made the exiled ætheling his heir — the last chance of an undisputed succession within the Saxon royal house; negotiations had begun with Bishop Ealdred's 1054 mission.

events.label: Arrived in England with his wife and children
events.labelCn: 携妻儿抵达英格兰
events.note: Edward finally arrived in England in 1057 with Agatha and their children — including the young Margaret, later queen of Scotland.

events.label: Death within days of arrival, before meeting the king
events.labelCn: 抵达数日后去世，未能面见国王
events.note: Edward died on 19 April 1057, within a few days of arriving in England, without meeting Edward the Confessor; he was buried in Old St Paul's Cathedral. The cause is not recorded.

sourceNote: Life is poorly documented: birth c. 1016; exile in Sweden, then (per most accounts) Hungary; recalled c. 1056; died 19 April 1057 days after arriving in England.
notes: Son of Edmund Ironside and Ealdgyth; his life between 1016 and 1057 is poorly documented and partly speculative. Sent to Sweden after Cnut's conquest, he was raised — per most accounts — at the court of King Stephen I of Hungary (some reconstructions say Kiev) and was recalled by Edward the Confessor as heir in 1056, only to die days after his return. His wife Agatha (origins disputed) and children Christina and Edgar the Ætheling are not in the roster.

deathCause.summary: Died within days of returning to England; cause not recorded
deathCause.detail: Edward arrived in England in 1057 after being recalled as heir by Edward the Confessor, but died within a few days, on 19 April 1057, before meeting the king. The cause is not recorded in contemporary sources; some later writers have suspected foul play, but there is no evidence of murder. He was buried in Old St Paul's Cathedral.
deathCause.summaryCn: 返回英格兰数日内去世，死因未载
deathCause.detailCn: 1057年，爱德华应忏悔者爱德华之召回国出任继承人，但抵达后数日内（4月19日）便去世，未能面见国王。当代史料未记载死因；后世个别记载怀疑他遭暗害，但并无证据。他被葬于老圣保罗大教堂。

fullNameCn: 流亡者爱德华

events.label: Birth in Hungary (c. 1045)
events.labelCn: 在匈牙利出生（约1045年）
events.note: Margaret was born in the Kingdom of Hungary about 1045, during her family's exile; the exact year is uncertain.

events.label: Came to England with her family after her father's death
events.labelCn: 父亲去世后随家人来到英格兰
events.note: The family was recalled to England in 1057, but her father Edward the Exile died immediately after landing; Margaret then resided at the English court.

events.label: Marriage to Malcolm III of Scotland
events.labelCn: 与苏格兰国王马尔科姆三世结婚
events.note: Margaret married the widowed Malcolm III in 1070 and became Queen of Scotland; the marriage linked the Anglo-Saxon royal house with the Scottish crown.

events.label: Church reforms in Scotland (Easter observance, Lenten fast, synods)
events.labelCn: 推动苏格兰教会改革（复活节习俗、斋戒、宗教会议）
events.note: Margaret instigated religious reform: she changed Lenten observance to begin on Ash Wednesday, abolished the Saturday Sabbath rest, and held synods to correct church practice.

events.label: Invited the Benedictines to Dunfermline
events.labelCn: 邀请本笃会修士至邓弗姆林
events.note: In 1072 Margaret invited the Benedictine order to Dunfermline, founding the priory that became Dunfermline Abbey, her burial place.

events.label: Restored Iona Abbey
events.labelCn: 重修艾奥纳修道院
events.note: Margaret restored the ancient abbey of Iona, and established pilgrim ferries at Queensferry and North Berwick.

events.label: Battle of Alnwick; husband Malcolm III and son Edward killed
events.labelCn: 阿尼克战役；丈夫马尔科姆三世与长子爱德华阵亡
events.note: On 13 November 1093 Malcolm III and her eldest son Edward were killed at the Battle of Alnwick during an invasion of Northumbria.

events.label: Death at Edinburgh Castle; buried at Dunfermline
events.labelCn: 在爱丁堡城堡去世，葬于邓弗姆林
events.note: Margaret died at Edinburgh Castle on 16 November 1093, three days after the deaths of her husband and eldest son, reportedly of grief; she was buried before the high altar at Dunfermline Abbey.

events.label: Canonised by Pope Innocent IV
events.labelCn: 被教皇英诺森四世封圣
events.note: Pope Innocent IV canonised Margaret in 1250; her remains were reinterred at Dunfermline on 19 June 1250.

sourceNote: Born c. 1045 in Hungary; married Malcolm III in 1070; died 16 November 1093 at Edinburgh Castle; canonised 1250.
notes: Daughter of Edward the Exile and Agatha; granddaughter of Edmund Ironside. Married Malcolm III of Scotland c. 1070; renowned for piety and church reform (Dunfermline, Iona) and canonised in 1250. Her piety is well documented in the biography by her confessor Turgot; hagiographic miracle stories are omitted here. Her husband Malcolm III and children other than Matilda of Scotland are not in the roster. The Scottish paternal line is intentionally not yet modeled.

deathCause.summary: Died at Edinburgh Castle, reportedly of grief, days after her husband and son were killed
deathCause.detail: Malcolm III and her eldest son Edward were killed at the Battle of Alnwick on 13 November 1093; Margaret died at Edinburgh Castle on 16 November 1093, reportedly of grief. She was buried before the high altar at Dunfermline Abbey.
deathCause.summaryCn: 丈夫与长子阵亡数日后在爱丁堡城堡去世，据载忧伤而逝
deathCause.detailCn: 1093年11月13日，马尔科姆三世与长子爱德华在阿尼克战役中阵亡；玛格丽特于11月16日在爱丁堡城堡去世，据载因忧伤过度。她葬于邓弗姆林修道院主祭坛前。

fullNameCn: 苏格兰的圣玛格丽特

fullName: Matilda of Scotland, Queen of England
fullNameCn: 苏格兰的玛蒂尔达，英格兰王后
deathPlaceCn: 英格兰伦敦威斯敏斯特宫
notes: Mother of Empress Matilda; christened Edith and took the regnal name Matilda at her coronation. Known as 'Good Queen Maud'. Acted as regent of England during Henry I's absences in 1104, 1107, 1108 and 1111. An attempted sainthood was never completed.

deathCause.detail: Matilda died at Westminster Palace on 1 May 1118, aged about 37-38. No violent cause is recorded; the precise illness is not documented.
deathCause.detailCn: 玛蒂尔达于1118年5月1日在威斯敏斯特宫去世，享年约37至38岁。史料未记载暴力死因，具体疾病不详。

events.label: Birth of Edith (later Matilda) at Dunfermline
events.labelCn: 埃迪丝（后来的玛蒂尔达）在邓弗姆林出生
events.note: Born c. 1080 in Dunfermline, Scotland; christened Edith (Eadgyth). Exact date unknown.

events.label: Marriage to Henry I at Westminster Abbey
events.labelCn: 在威斯敏斯特教堂与亨利一世成婚
events.note: Married 11 November 1100, officiated by Archbishop Anselm; Edith took the regnal name Matilda.

events.label: Crowned Queen of England
events.labelCn: 加冕为英格兰王后
events.note: Crowned on her wedding day, 11 November 1100.

events.label: Birth of Empress Matilda
events.labelCn: 女皇玛蒂尔达出生
events.note: Daughter Matilda (later Holy Roman Empress and claimant to England) born 7 February 1102.

events.label: Birth of William Adelin
events.labelCn: 威廉·阿德林出生
events.note: Son and heir William born 5 August 1103; he drowned in the White Ship disaster of 1120.

events.label: Regent of England during Henry I's absences
events.labelCn: 在亨利一世外出期间摄政英格兰
events.note: Acted as regent of England in 1104, 1107, 1108 and 1111 while Henry campaigned in Normandy and France; head of Henry's court during his absence.

events.label: Death of Matilda of Scotland
events.labelCn: 苏格兰的玛蒂尔达去世
events.note: Died at Westminster Palace; buried in Westminster Abbey near Edward the Confessor.

fullName: Elizabeth of York, Queen of England
fullNameCn: 约克的伊丽莎白，英格兰王后
notes: Daughter of Edward IV. Her marriage to Henry VII united the Houses of York and Lancaster. She died of a postpartum infection on her 37th birthday, eleven days after giving birth to Katherine Tudor; Henry VII never remarried.

deathCause.detail: Elizabeth died on 11 February 1503 at the Tower of London, eleven days after giving birth to her last child, Katherine Tudor, succumbing to a postpartum infection.
deathCause.detailCn: 伊丽莎白于1503年2月11日在伦敦塔去世，在生下最后一个孩子凯瑟琳·都铎十一天后死于产后感染。

events.label: Birth of Elizabeth of York at Westminster
events.labelCn: 约克的伊丽莎白在威斯敏斯特出生
events.note: Born 11 February 1466 at the Palace of Westminster, eldest child of Edward IV and Elizabeth Woodville.

events.label: Tudor Victory at Bosworth
events.labelCn: 博斯沃思之战中的都铎胜利

events.label: Marriage to Henry VII
events.labelCn: 与亨利七世成婚

events.label: Birth of Arthur, Prince of Wales
events.labelCn: 威尔士亲王亚瑟出生
events.note: First son Arthur born 20 September 1486, eight months after the royal wedding.

events.label: Coronation as Queen of England
events.labelCn: 加冕为英格兰王后

events.label: Birth of Henry VIII
events.labelCn: 亨利八世出生

events.label: Marriage of Prince Arthur to Catherine of Aragon
events.labelCn: 亚瑟王子与阿拉贡的凯瑟琳成婚
events.note: Dynastic alliance with Spain at St Paul's Cathedral; Arthur died five months later.

events.label: Death of Elizabeth of York
events.labelCn: 约克的伊丽莎白去世

fullNameCn: 英格兰国王亨利七世
notes: Tudor paternal line intentionally not modeled. Founder of the Tudor royal line in this tree. Born at Pembroke Castle in Wales on 28 January 1457; only child of Margaret Beaufort (aged 13) and Edmund Tudor, who died before his birth.

deathCause.detail: Henry VII died at Richmond Palace of tuberculosis, after declining health; no violent cause is recorded.
deathCause.detailCn: 亨利七世在健康恶化后因肺结核去世于里士满宫；无暴力死因记载。

events.label: Battle of Bosworth Field
events.labelCn: 博斯沃思原野战役
events.note: Henry defeated and killed Richard III on 22 August 1485, ending the Wars of the Roses.

events.label: Became King of England
events.labelCn: 成为英格兰国王
events.note: Henry claimed the crown on the field of battle by right of conquest, backdated to 21 August 1485; Parliament confirmed his title in November 1485.

events.label: Coronation as King of England
events.labelCn: 加冕为英格兰国王
events.note: Crowned at Westminster Abbey on 30 October 1485.

events.label: Marriage to Elizabeth of York
events.labelCn: 与约克的伊丽莎白成婚
events.note: Married Elizabeth of York at Westminster Abbey on 18 January 1486, uniting the Houses of Lancaster and York and securing Yorkist acceptance of his reign.

events.label: Battle of Stoke Field
events.labelCn: 斯托克原野战役
events.note: Final battle of the Wars of the Roses: Yorkist rebels backing the pretender Lambert Simnel were crushed and John de la Pole, Earl of Lincoln, was killed.

events.label: Treaty of Medina del Campo
events.labelCn: 《梅迪纳德尔坎波条约》
events.note: Signed in March 1489 with Spain; betrothed Arthur, Prince of Wales, to Catherine of Aragon.

events.label: Treaty of Etaples
events.labelCn: 《埃塔普勒条约》
events.note: Signed on 3 November 1492 after Henry's brief invasion of France; Charles VIII paid a large indemnity and agreed not to shelter pretenders.

events.label: Intercursus Magnus with Burgundy
events.labelCn: 与勃艮第签订《大通商条约》
events.note: Signed in February 1496; restored the wool and cloth trade with the Burgundian Netherlands after the trade embargo.

events.label: Perkin Warbeck's rising in Cornwall
events.labelCn: 珀金·沃贝克在康沃尔登陆起事
events.note: Warbeck, who claimed to be Richard of York (one of the Princes in the Tower), landed in Cornwall in September 1497 and was quickly captured; he was executed in 1499.

events.label: Death of Arthur, Prince of Wales
events.labelCn: 王储亚瑟去世
events.note: Arthur died at Ludlow Castle on 2 April 1502, very likely of the sweating sickness, making the future Henry VIII the heir.

events.label: Margaret Tudor weds James IV of Scotland
events.labelCn: 长女玛格丽特与苏格兰詹姆斯四世联姻
events.note: Margaret married James IV on 8 August 1503 under the Treaty of Perpetual Peace (1502); the match later carried the Stuart claim to the English throne.

events.label: Death of Henry VII
events.labelCn: 亨利七世去世
events.note: Henry died at Richmond Palace of tuberculosis on 21 April 1509 and was succeeded by his son Henry VIII.

fullNameCn: 英格兰国王亨利八世
notes: Only the Mary I and Elizabeth I branches are modeled here; his six wives and his other children (including Edward VI) remain outside this pass, so marriages are covered as events rather than as relationship links.

deathCause.detail: Henry VIII died at Whitehall Palace after years of serious health problems, including severe leg ulcers, a gangrenous leg wound from a 1536 jousting accident, and declining mobility; the exact cause of death is uncertain.
deathCause.detailCn: 亨利八世在多年严重健康问题后于白厅宫去世，包括严重的腿部溃疡、1536年比武事故造成的腿部坏疽以及行动能力衰退；确切死因尚无定论。

events.label: Became King of England
events.labelCn: 成为英格兰国王
events.note: Succeeded on the death of his father Henry VII on 21 April 1509.

events.label: Marriage to Catherine of Aragon
events.labelCn: 与阿拉贡的凯瑟琳成婚
events.note: Married Catherine, widow of his elder brother Arthur, at Greenwich on 11 June 1509; they were crowned together on 24 June.

events.label: Coronation as King of England
events.labelCn: 加冕为英格兰国王
events.note: Crowned at Westminster Abbey together with Catherine of Aragon on 24 June 1509.

events.label: The King's Great Matter begins
events.labelCn: “国王的大事”——亨利谋求废除与凯瑟琳的婚姻
events.note: Henry sought the annulment of his marriage to Catherine of Aragon, citing her earlier marriage to Arthur; the Pope's refusal set the course towards the break with Rome.

events.label: Marriage to Anne Boleyn
events.labelCn: 与安妮·博林成婚
events.note: Secret marriage to the pregnant Anne Boleyn in London; Cranmer's court declared the Catherine marriage void on 23 May 1533.

events.label: Annulment of marriage to Catherine of Aragon
events.labelCn: 宣布与阿拉贡的凯瑟琳的婚姻无效
events.note: Archbishop Cranmer's court at Dunstable declared the marriage to Catherine invalid; Catherine never accepted the ruling.

events.label: Birth of Elizabeth I
events.labelCn: 伊丽莎白（后来的伊丽莎白一世）出生
events.note: Anne Boleyn gave birth to Elizabeth at Greenwich Palace on 7 September 1533; Henry's disappointment over a daughter weakened Anne's position.

events.label: Act of Supremacy
events.labelCn: 《至尊法案》
events.note: The First Act of Supremacy (royal assent 3 November 1534) declared Henry Supreme Head of the Church of England; Pope Clement VII's excommunication of Henry was not made official until later.

events.label: Execution of Anne Boleyn
events.labelCn: 安妮·博林被处决
events.note: Anne was beheaded on Tower Green on 19 May 1536 after conviction for treason and adultery on charges widely regarded as engineered.

events.label: Dissolution of the Monasteries begins
events.labelCn: 解散修道院运动开始
events.note: The First Suppression Act (1536) closed the smaller religious houses; the Second Suppression Act (1539) dissolved the rest, with their wealth and lands seized by the Crown.

events.label: Pilgrimage of Grace
events.labelCn: 求恩巡礼叛乱
events.note: A major northern rising, begun in October 1536, against the dissolution of the monasteries and religious changes; its leaders were pardoned and then executed in 1537.

events.label: Birth of Edward VI
events.labelCn: 爱德华（后来的爱德华六世）出生
events.note: Jane Seymour bore the long-awaited male heir on 12 October 1537; she died of complications on 24 October 1537.

events.label: Marriage to Anne of Cleves
events.labelCn: 与克利夫斯的安妮成婚
events.note: Political marriage sealed on the strength of a Holbein portrait; the marriage was never consummated and was annulled on 9 July 1540.

events.label: Annulment of marriage to Anne of Cleves
events.labelCn: 宣布与克利夫斯的安妮的婚姻无效
events.note: Annulled on grounds of non-consummation and an alleged pre-contract; Anne accepted a generous settlement and outlived Henry.

events.label: Became King of Ireland
events.labelCn: 成为爱尔兰国王
events.note: Crown of Ireland Act: passed by the Irish Parliament in 1541, with royal assent following in 1542; the event is dated per the original record.

events.label: Death of Henry VIII
events.labelCn: 亨利八世去世
events.note: Henry died at Whitehall Palace on 28 January 1547 after years of declining health and was succeeded by Edward VI.

events.label: Battle of the Spurs
events.labelCn: 马刺战役

fullNameCn: 英格兰女王玛丽一世
notes: Daughter of Henry VIII; her mother Catherine of Aragon is intentionally not modeled in this pass. Died during an influenza epidemic; modern scholars suspect ovarian cysts or uterine cancer. 'Bloody Mary' is a posthumous epithet tied to the Marian persecutions.

deathCause.detail: Mary died at St James's Palace on 17 November 1558, aged 42, during an influenza epidemic; modern scholars suspect ovarian cysts or uterine cancer as the underlying cause. Not a violent death.
deathCause.detailCn: 玛丽于1558年11月17日在圣詹姆斯宫去世，享年42岁，正值流感流行期间；现代学者推测潜在死因可能是卵巢囊肿或子宫癌。非暴力死亡。

events.label: Birth of Mary at Greenwich Palace
events.labelCn: 玛丽在格林尼治宫出生
events.note: Only child of Henry VIII and Catherine of Aragon to survive infancy.

events.label: Declared illegitimate and removed from succession
events.labelCn: 被宣告为私生女并排除出继承序列
events.note: In May 1533 Cranmer annulled Henry VIII's marriage to Catherine of Aragon; Mary was deemed illegitimate, styled 'The Lady Mary' and barred from the succession.

events.label: Restored to succession by the Third Succession Act
events.labelCn: 经《第三次继承法》恢复继承权
events.note: Henry VIII placed Mary after Edward in the line of succession, though she remained legally illegitimate.

events.label: Became Queen of England
events.labelCn: 成为英格兰女王

events.label: Coronation as Queen of England
events.labelCn: 加冕为英格兰女王

events.label: Wyatt's Rebellion in Kent
events.labelCn: 肯特郡怀亚特叛乱
events.note: January-February 1554: revolt led by Thomas Wyatt the Younger against Mary's planned marriage to Philip of Spain; suppressed in February, Wyatt executed.

events.label: Marriage to Philip of Spain
events.labelCn: 与西班牙的腓力成婚

events.label: Restoration of Papal Supremacy
events.labelCn: 恢复教皇至上权威
events.note: Existing event, dated: 30 November 1554 Cardinal Pole absolved Parliament in Mary's presence, ending the English schism with Rome.

events.label: Marian Persecutions begin (c. 280 burned)
events.labelCn: 玛丽宗教迫害开始（约280人被处火刑）
events.note: First burnings in February 1555; more than 280 Protestants were executed by burning by 1558. Factual record, kept neutral.

events.label: Loss of Calais to France
events.labelCn: 加来被法国攻陷
events.note: Existing event, dated: French forces took Calais in January 1558 (capitulation 7 January), England's last continental possession.

events.label: Death of Mary I
events.labelCn: 玛丽一世去世

events.label: Loss of Calais
events.labelCn: 失去加来

fullNameCn: 英格兰女王伊丽莎白一世
notes: Daughter of Henry VIII; her mother Anne Boleyn is intentionally not modeled in this pass. Last Tudor monarch. Never married, and died without issue; she was succeeded by James VI of Scotland.

deathCause.detail: Elizabeth died at Richmond Palace on 24 March 1603 after a period of declining health in the final months of her reign; the immediate cause of death is uncertain.
deathCause.detailCn: 伊丽莎白在其统治的最后数月健康状况持续衰退，于1603年3月24日在里士满宫去世；直接死因尚无定论。

events.label: Imprisoned in the Tower of London
events.labelCn: 因怀亚特叛乱受嫌被囚于伦敦塔
events.note: Suspected of involvement in Wyatt's Rebellion, Elizabeth was imprisoned in the Tower on 18 March 1554 and later held at Woodstock; she was released in 1555.

events.label: Became Queen of England
events.labelCn: 成为英格兰女王
events.note: Elizabeth succeeded on the death of her half-sister Mary I on 17 November 1558.

events.label: Coronation as Queen of England
events.labelCn: 加冕为英格兰女王
events.note: Crowned at Westminster Abbey on 15 January 1559.

events.label: Elizabethan Religious Settlement
events.labelCn: 伊丽莎白宗教和解
events.note: The Act of Supremacy (law from 8 May 1559) restored the royal supremacy and the Act of Uniformity established the 1559 Book of Common Prayer, defining the Protestant Church of England.

events.label: Poor Act of 1563
events.labelCn: 《1563年济贫法》
events.note: Early poor-relief legislation; further Acts followed in 1598 and 1601.

events.label: Mary, Queen of Scots flees to England
events.labelCn: 苏格兰女王玛丽逃入英格兰并被软禁
events.note: After her defeat at Langside in May 1568, Mary fled to England and was detained for nineteen years, becoming the focus of Catholic plots.

events.label: Papal excommunication of Elizabeth
events.labelCn: 教皇颁布诏书绝罚伊丽莎白
events.note: Pope Pius V issued Regnans in Excelsis on 25 February 1570, excommunicating Elizabeth and absolving English Catholics of allegiance to her.

events.label: Courtship of Francis, Duke of Anjou
events.labelCn: 安茹公爵弗朗索瓦的求婚
events.note: The last serious marriage negotiation; the courtship collapsed by 1581 and Elizabeth remained unmarried — the 'Virgin Queen'.

events.label: Treaty of Nonsuch with the Dutch
events.labelCn: 与荷兰签订《楠萨奇条约》
events.note: England pledged military support to the Dutch Revolt on 20 August 1585, provoking the Anglo-Spanish War.

events.label: Execution of Mary, Queen of Scots
events.labelCn: 处决苏格兰女王玛丽
events.note: Mary was beheaded at Fotheringhay Castle on 8 February 1587 after the Babington Plot; Elizabeth claimed the signed warrant had been sent without her knowledge.

events.label: Defeat of the Spanish Armada
events.labelCn: 击败西班牙无敌舰队
events.note: The Spanish Armada sailed in July 1588; English fire-ships scattered it off Gravelines on 28-29 July, and storms wrecked many of the surviving ships on the Irish coast.

events.label: Essex's Rebellion
events.labelCn: 埃塞克斯伯爵叛乱
events.note: Robert Devereux, Earl of Essex, led a failed rising in London on 8 February 1601 and was executed on 25 February.

events.label: Elizabethan Poor Law
events.labelCn: 伊丽莎白济贫法
events.note: The 1601 Elizabethan Poor Law consolidated earlier legislation (1563, 1598) and shaped English poor relief for centuries.

events.label: The Golden Speech
events.labelCn: 黄金演讲
events.note: Elizabeth's farewell speech to Parliament on 30 November 1601, affirming her bond with her subjects.

events.label: Death of Elizabeth I
events.labelCn: 伊丽莎白一世去世
events.note: Elizabeth died at Richmond Palace on 24 March 1603; James VI of Scotland succeeded as James I, ending the Tudor dynasty.

events.label: Count of Poitiers
events.labelCn: 成为普瓦捷伯爵
events.note: Effective start of his tenure as count of Poitiers. Ademar of Chabannes claims he was appointed in 840 and the EN succession box gives 835, but modern scholarship (following the death of Bishop Ebroin) regards 854 as most plausible.

events.label: Wounded at the Battle of Brissarthe
events.labelCn: 在布里斯萨特战役中负伤
events.note: Fighting Viking raiders at Brissarthe on 15 September 866; Robert the Strong was killed and Ramnulf was gravely wounded by an arrow.

events.label: Death of Ramnulf I
events.labelCn: 拉姆努尔夫一世去世
events.note: Died of his battle wounds at Poitiers about a month after Brissarthe (15 October 866 per French Wikipedia).

sourceNote: Early Ramnulfid genealogy and dates are partly uncertain: birth year 820 (FR infobox) or c. 825 (Settipani); the start of the countship is variously given as 835/840/854; the identities of his mother and wife (Adaltrude of Maine / Bilichilde) are uncertain. He was also a lay abbot of Saint-Hilaire (841-866).
notes: Founder of the House of Poitiers/Ramnulfids; son of Gerard, Count of Auvergne according to the cited genealogy. NOTE: the EN article is titled 'Ranulf I of Aquitaine' — the previously stored URL with the 'Ramnulf' spelling returns 404 and has been corrected.

deathCause.summary: Died of wounds from the Battle of Brissarthe
deathCause.detail: Fought the Vikings at Brissarthe (15 September 866) alongside Robert the Strong, who was killed; Ramnulf was wounded by an arrow and died of his wounds in Poitiers around 15 October 866.
deathCause.summaryCn: 死于布里斯萨特战役所受的箭伤
deathCause.detailCn: 866年9月15日与罗伯特·强者一同在布里斯萨特与维京人作战；罗伯特阵亡，拉姆努尔夫中箭重伤，约10月15日在普瓦捷伤重不治。

fullNameCn: 普瓦捷伯爵拉姆努尔夫一世

events.label: Count of Poitiers after his father's death
events.labelCn: 继承普瓦捷伯爵
events.note: Succeeded his father Ramnulf I. The EN article gives 866, French Wikipedia gives 877 and its succession box 886-890 — the start date varies by source.

events.label: Styled himself King of Aquitaine
events.labelCn: 自称阿基坦国王
events.note: After the death of Charles the Fat in 888 he styled himself King of Aquitaine (per the Annales Fuldenses) and refused to recognize Odo as king; the claim lasted until 889 or his death. French Wikipedia instead presents him as styling himself duke (dux maximae partis Aquitaniae), so the royal title is contested.

events.label: Death of Ramnulf II
events.labelCn: 拉姆努尔夫二世去世
events.note: Died at Paris on 5 August 890; French Wikipedia reports he may have been poisoned ('peut-etre empoisonne'). His legitimate son Ramnulf III was short-lived, so the illegitimate Ebalus Manzer carried the line.

sourceNote: The claim to be King of Aquitaine was short-lived and contested: it rests mainly on the Annales Fuldenses, and French Wikipedia describes only a self-styled ducal title (888-890). Count-of-Poitiers start date varies (866/877/886). He took custody of the child Charles (later Charles the Simple) after 888.
notes: Son of Ramnulf I; father of the genealogical Ramnulf III branch and of the illegitimate Ebalus Manzer. His wife Ermengarde is otherwise unrecorded and even the marriage is uncertain; the identity of his mother is debated (Bilichilde of Maine, a Guilhemide princess, or another wife of Ramnulf I).

deathCause.detail: Ramnulf II died at Paris on 5 August 890. French Wikipedia suggests he may have been poisoned, but the cause is not confirmed and the EN article gives no cause of death.
deathCause.detailCn: 拉姆努尔夫二世于890年8月5日在巴黎去世。法语维基百科推测其可能被毒杀，但死因未获确认，英文维基百科未记载死因。

fullNameCn: 普瓦捷伯爵拉姆努尔夫二世

sourceNote: Genealogical entry; dates and detailed biography are not securely established in the cited overview.
notes: Shown as a branch of Ramnulf II in the House of Poitiers genealogy, not as the direct father of Ebalus.
fullNameCn: 阿基坦的拉姆努尔夫三世

events.label: Count of Poitiers after Ramnulf II's death
events.labelCn: 继承普瓦捷伯爵
events.note: As the illegitimate son of Ramnulf II he took Poitou after his father's death, but his right to rule was challenged because he was a bastard.

events.label: Aymar seizes Poitiers; Ebalus goes into exile
events.labelCn: 埃马尔夺取普瓦捷，埃布勒斯流亡
events.note: In 892 Aymar, backed by King Odo of France, overthrew Ebalus; he fled to the safety of his father's allies William the Pious and Gerald of Aurillac.

events.label: Recovered Poitiers with William the Pious
events.labelCn: 在虔诚者威廉支持下收复普瓦捷
events.note: Retook Poitiers in 902 with an army lent by the distant relative William the Pious and was formally invested as Count of Poitou by Charles the Simple; he conquered the Limousin in 904.

events.label: Fought Rollo at the Battle of Chartres
events.labelCn: 参与沙特尔之战抗击罗洛
events.note: Participated in the campaign that defeated Rollo's Vikings at Chartres in 911 (FR Wikipedia; the exact date, 20 July or 21 August 911, varies by source).

events.label: Duke of Aquitaine and Auvergne
events.labelCn: 成为阿基坦公爵兼奥弗涅伯爵
events.note: After the deaths of William the Younger and his brother Acfred, Ebalus inherited the duchy of Aquitaine and the counties of Berry, Auvergne and Velay (FR dates this to 927, EN to 928). He was stripped of Berry in 929, and in 932 King Raoul transferred the duchy of Aquitaine and Auvergne to Raymond Pons of Toulouse.

events.label: Death of Ebalus Manzer
events.labelCn: 埃布勒斯·曼泽尔去世
events.note: Death year given as 934 in this project's data; Wikipedia gives 934/935 (infobox 935). No cause of death is recorded.

sourceNote: Wikipedia identifies Ebalus as the illegitimate son of Ranulf II; the exact maternal line is not supplied ('Manzer' is a Hebrew word meaning bastard). Birth c. 870, uncertain. Titles: Count of Poitou 890-892 and 902-934; Duke of Aquitaine 927/928-932. Death year 934/935.
notes: His line leads to the later House of Poitiers dukes and Eleanor of Aquitaine. NOTE on titles: the previous record dated his countship from 927; sources show he held Poitou continuously from 902 (after an earlier 890-892 tenure), so the entry was corrected, and the Duchy of Aquitaine (927-932) added.

deathCause.detail: No cause of death is recorded for Ebalus Manzer. The year is given as 934 in this project's data; Wikipedia gives 934/935 (infobox 935).
deathCause.detailCn: 埃布勒斯·曼泽尔的死因没有记载。项目数据记作934年；维基百科记载为934/935年（信息框为935年）。

fullNameCn: 普瓦捷伯爵埃布勒斯·曼泽尔

fullName: Guilhem III Towhead, Count of Poitiers

events.label: Count of Poitiers
events.labelCn: 成为普瓦捷伯爵
events.note: Succeeded his father Ebalus Manzer at Poitiers. Birth year 913 per the infobox (915 in the page's succession box); born when his father was already middle-aged.

events.label: Marriage to Gerloc of Normandy
events.labelCn: 与诺曼底的热洛丝结婚
events.note: Married Gerloc (known as Adele), daughter of Rollo of Normandy, forging a Norman alliance. The c. 936 date comes from the less reliable Dudo of Saint-Quentin and is tentative. (Gerloc is not in the roster, so no spouse link is recorded.)

events.label: Repulsed Hugh the Great's invasion
events.labelCn: 击退大胡子于格的入侵
events.note: Hugh the Great, reconciled with King Louis IV, was granted the duchies of Burgundy and Aquitaine and attacked Aquitaine with royal support; William defeated them.

events.label: Defeated at the siege of Poitiers
events.labelCn: 普瓦捷围城战中失利
events.note: King Lothair and Hugh the Great besieged Poitiers in August 955; the city held out, but William gave battle and was routed. After Hugh's death, Hugh Capet was named Duke of Aquitaine but never took up the fief.

events.label: Ducal title recognized at the royal court
events.labelCn: 获王室认可为阿基坦公爵
events.note: He claimed the duchy from his father's death, but the royal chancery recognized the title only around 962 (the article's lead dates the title to 959); he was also given the abbey of Saint-Hilaire-le-Grand.

events.label: Death of Guilhem III
events.labelCn: 吉勒姆三世去世
events.note: Died 3 April 963 at Saint-Maixent-l'Ecole and was buried at the Abbey of Saint-Cyprien, Poitiers; no cause of death is recorded.

sourceNote: Wikipedia notes that he was called Count of the Duchy of Aquitaine or Count Palatine, but not unambiguously Duke of Aquitaine. Uncertain: birth year 913 vs 915; start of the ducal title 959 vs 962; marriage date c. 936 tentative; the filiation of his (possible) daughter Adelaide is disputed.
notes: Occitanized display name; English and French forms remain in alsoKnownAs. 'Towhead' (Tete d'etoupe) refers to the flaxen colour of his hair, not to baldness; the Chinese nickname has been corrected from 'bald head' to 'flaxen-haired' accordingly.

deathCause.summary: Died at Saint-Maixent-l'Ecole; no cause recorded
deathCause.detail: Guilhem III died 3 April 963 at Saint-Maixent-l'Ecole and was buried at the Abbey of Saint-Cyprien in Poitiers; the sources record no cause of death.
deathCause.summaryCn: 在圣迈克桑莱科莱去世，死因不详
deathCause.detailCn: 吉勒姆三世于963年4月3日在圣迈克桑莱科莱去世，葬于普瓦捷的圣西普里安修道院；史料未记载死因。

fullNameCn: 普瓦捷伯爵吉勒姆三世·亚麻头

fullName: Guilhem IV Fierabras, Count of Poitiers

events.label: Count of Poitiers and Duke of Aquitaine
events.labelCn: 继承普瓦捷伯爵与阿基坦公爵
events.note: Succeeded his father Guilhem III, who retired to the abbey of Saint-Cyprien in Poitiers.

events.label: Marriage to Emma of Blois
events.labelCn: 与布卢瓦的埃玛结婚
events.note: Married Emma, daughter of Theobald I of Blois and Luitgarde of Vermandois. The marriage was stormy: Emma banished his mistresses and they separated twice.

events.label: Resisted King Hugh Capet's invasion
events.labelCn: 抵御国王于格·卡佩的入侵
events.note: Refused to recognize Hugh Capet (his brother-in-law), who invaded Aquitaine; the royal army was defeated on the plain of the Loire. He also sheltered Louis, son of Charles of Lower Lorraine, the last Carolingian heir.

events.label: Death of Guilhem IV
events.labelCn: 吉勒姆四世去世
events.note: Died 3 February 994 and was buried at Maillezais Cathedral; an alternative date of 5 February 995 also appears (from Owen). He had retired to a monastery c. 990, leaving Emma to rule Aquitaine in the name of their son William until 1004.

sourceNote: The numbering differs between the counts of Poitiers and dukes of Aquitaine. Death date disputed: 3 February 994 (EN and FR infoboxes) vs 5 February 995 (alternative). Birth year c. 937 (c. 935 per FR). The title's end year is variously given as 990 (retirement), 993 or 995 depending on the source.
notes: Occitanized display name; Fierabras means strong-armed/iron arm in the traditional epithet (the EN article glosses it as 'Proud Arm' from Fier-a-bras). His death year has been updated from 995 to 994 following the EN/FR Wikipedia infoboxes, with the 995 alternative flagged.

deathCause.detail: No cause of death is recorded for Guilhem IV. He died 3 February 994 and was buried at Maillezais Cathedral, though an alternative date of 5 February 995 appears in some works; he had retired to a monastery c. 990 with Emma as regent.
deathCause.detailCn: 吉勒姆四世死因没有记载。他于994年2月3日去世，葬于马耶宰大教堂；部分著作记为995年2月5日。约990年他已隐退修道院，由埃玛摄政。

fullNameCn: 普瓦捷伯爵吉勒姆四世·铁臂

fullName: Guilhem V the Great, Count of Poitiers

events.label: Duke of Aquitaine and Count of Poitiers
events.labelCn: 继承阿基坦公爵与普瓦捷伯爵
events.note: Succeeded his father Guilhem IV, who had retired to a monastery; his mother Emma of Blois acted as regent in his name until 1004.

events.label: Personal rule begins
events.labelCn: 开始亲政
events.note: Took up personal rule when his mother's regency ended in 1004.

events.label: Defeated by Viking raiders
events.labelCn: 被维京人击败
events.note: Suffered a defeat against Viking invaders in 1006.

events.label: Founded Maillezais Abbey
events.labelCn: 创建马耶宰修道院
events.note: Founded Maillezais Abbey (1010) and Bourgueil Abbey, rebuilt Poitiers cathedral after a fire, and supported the Peace and Truce of God movements — the basis of his reputation for piety.

events.label: Treaty with Fulk Nerra of Anjou
events.labelCn: 与安茹的富尔克订立条约
events.note: After losing the Loudunais and Mirebalais to Fulk Nerra, a treaty negotiated by Fulbert of Chartres (1020) defined their vassal-suzerain obligations; he also ceded Confolens, Ruffec and Chabanais to William II of Angouleme.

events.label: Declined the crown of Italy
events.labelCn: 婉拒意大利王位
events.note: After Emperor Henry II's death, Italian nobles offered him the kingdom of Italy; he visited Italy (1024-1025) but found the situation unfavorable and renounced the crown for himself and his heirs.

events.label: Death of Guilhem V
events.labelCn: 吉勒姆五世去世
events.note: Died at Maillezais Abbey, which he had founded and where he is buried, on the last (or second-to-last) day of January 1030; 'his reign ended in peace.' No cause of death is recorded.

sourceNote: The Ramnulfid overview identifies William V as the father of William VI, Odo, William VII and William VIII branches. Uncertain: death day (30 or 31 January 1030); the death place was corrected from Poitiers to Maillezais Abbey per the EN article; the first wife's name is given as Adalemode of Limoges (not 'Sancha').
notes: Important patron of learning and culture in Aquitaine; do not collapse his four sons into a single succession chain. He received ambassadors from Emperor Henry II, Alfonso V of Leon, Canute the Great and King Robert of France, and traveled widely, 'annually visiting Rome or Spain as a pilgrim.' NOTE: the Chinese nickname 'the Great' has been corrected from 'Grand Duke' to 'the Great one'.

deathCause.summary: Died at Maillezais Abbey; no cause recorded
deathCause.detail: Guilhem V died at Maillezais Abbey (which he founded) on the last or second-to-last day of January 1030, 'his reign ended in peace'; no cause of death is recorded.
deathCause.summaryCn: 在马耶宰修道院去世，死因不详
deathCause.detailCn: 吉勒姆五世于1030年1月最后一天（或倒数第二天）在他创建的马耶宰修道院去世，'统治在和平中结束'；死因没有记载。

fullNameCn: 普瓦捷伯爵吉勒姆五世·伟大者

fullName: Guilhem VI the Fat, Count of Poitiers
sourceNote: Dates are incomplete in the cited overview.
notes: Eldest son of William V; count of Poitiers from 1030 to 1038.
fullNameCn: 普瓦捷伯爵吉勒姆六世·肥胖者

fullName: Odo of Gascony, Count of Poitiers
sourceNote: Half-brother of William VI according to the Ramnulfid genealogy.
notes: A collateral succession branch; not the father of William VII or William VIII.
fullNameCn: 普瓦捷伯爵加斯科涅的奥多

events.label: Duke of Aquitaine after Odo's death
events.labelCn: 在奥多死后继承阿基坦公爵
events.note: Succeeded his half-brother Odo of Gascony, who was killed in battle at Mauze; Guilhem VII recovered his patrimony but did not succeed in occupying Gascony. (His sister Agnes's marriage to Emperor Henry III made him the emperor's brother-in-law.)

events.label: War with Geoffroy Martel; siege of Saumur
events.labelCn: 与若弗鲁瓦·马特尔开战并围攻索米尔
events.note: His mother Agnes had remarried Geoffroy Martel, Count of Anjou, who refused to return territories taken under earlier dukes; Guilhem took up arms and besieged Geoffroy at Saumur.

events.label: Death of Guilhem VII
events.labelCn: 吉勒姆七世去世
events.note: Died of dysentery while besieging Saumur in autumn 1058; succeeded by his younger half-brother Guilhem VIII. The two daughters sometimes attributed to him (Clementia, Agnes) are only hypothesized.

sourceNote: Also known as Peter William; half-brother of William VI and William VIII. His wife Ermesinde is of uncertain origins, and the two daughters attributed to the couple are only hypothesized. Death: autumn 1058, of dysentery at the siege of Saumur; no exact date.
notes: The direct dynastic line to Guilhem IX runs through his brother Guilhem VIII, not through Guilhem VII. Nicknamed 'the Eagle' (Aigret) or 'the Bold' (le Hardi).
