deathCause.summary: Died of dysentery at the siege of Saumur
deathCause.detail: Guilhem VII died of dysentery in autumn 1058 while besieging Geoffroy Martel of Anjou at Saumur; no exact day is recorded.
deathCause.summaryCn: 在围攻索米尔时死于痢疾
deathCause.detailCn: 吉勒姆七世于1058年秋在围攻安茹伯爵若弗鲁瓦·马特尔所在的索米尔时死于痢疾，具体日期未记载。

fullNameCn: 阿基坦公爵吉勒姆七世

events.label: Duke of Gascony
events.labelCn: 成为加斯科涅公爵
events.note: Became Duke of Gascony in 1052, succeeding Bernard II Tumapaler; Gascony had come into Aquitanian orbit through his father's marriage to Prisca of Gascony.

events.label: Duke of Aquitaine and Count of Poitiers
events.labelCn: 继承阿基坦公爵与普瓦捷伯爵
events.note: Succeeded his brother Guilhem VII, who died at the siege of Saumur.

events.label: Divorce from Garsende of Perigord
events.labelCn: 与佩里戈尔的加森德离婚
events.note: Divorced his first wife Garsende (November 1058), reportedly for infertility; she became a nun at Saintes.

events.label: Siege of Barbastro
events.labelCn: 围攻巴尔巴斯特罗
events.note: Co-led the allied army aiding Ramiro I of Aragon at the Siege of Barbastro (1064), the first campaign organized by the papacy (Pope Alexander II) and a precursor of the Crusades; the city fell but was lost again within a few years.

events.label: Divorce from Matoeda
events.labelCn: 与马托埃达离婚
events.note: Divorced his second wife Matoeda in May 1068; their daughter Agnes later married Alfonso VI of Castile.

events.label: Pilgrimage to Rome for papal recognition
events.labelCn: 赴罗马寻求教宗认可
events.note: Visited Rome in the early 1070s to win papal recognition for the children of his third marriage to Hildegarde of Burgundy (his cousin), since the Church had initially considered them illegitimate. (Year approximate: 1071-1074.)

events.label: Death of Guilhem VIII
events.labelCn: 吉勒姆八世去世
events.note: Died 25 September 1086 at Chizé, aged about 61; no cause of death recorded. His daughters' marriages to Iberian kings (Alfonso VI of Castile, Peter I of Aragon) cemented Spanish alliances.

sourceNote: Born Gui-Geoffroi; younger brother of William VII and father of William IX. Birth year c. 1025; divorce dates are precise (November 1058, May 1068); death 25 September 1086 at Chizé.
notes: Occitanized display name Guilhem VIII; the direct father link to existing Guilhem IX is now represented by UUID. His third wife Hildegarde of Burgundy was his cousin, which is why the children of that marriage initially needed papal recognition.

deathCause.summary: Died at Chizé; no cause recorded
deathCause.detail: Guilhem VIII died 25 September 1086 at Chizé, aged about 61; no cause of death is recorded in the sources.
deathCause.detailCn: 吉勒姆八世于1086年9月25日在希泽去世，享年约61岁；史料未记载死因。

fullNameCn: 阿基坦公爵吉勒姆八世

fullName: Hugues Capet, King of the Franks
deathPlaceCn: 莱瑞夫（普拉斯维尔附近），西法兰克王国

events.label: Succeeded Hugh the Great as Duke of the Franks
events.labelCn: 继承强者于格成为法兰克公爵
events.note: Hugh the Great died in 956; Hugh Capet succeeded him as Duke of the Franks (Duke of Francia) and Count of Paris.

events.label: Marriage to Adelaide of Aquitaine
events.labelCn: 与阿基坦的阿德莱德成婚
events.note: Daughter of William III Towhead, Count of Poitou; date approximate (c. 969-970).

events.label: Defence of Paris against Otto II
events.labelCn: 抵御奥托二世对巴黎的围攻
events.note: Helped repel the imperial army of Emperor Otto II besieging Paris; his personal role is uncertain.

events.label: Elected King of the Franks at Senlis
events.labelCn: 在桑利斯被选为法兰克人国王
events.note: Assembly at Senlis promoted by Archbishop Adalberon of Reims; the exact day is traditional.

events.label: Coronation at Noyon
events.labelCn: 在努瓦永加冕
events.note: Wikipedia gives the coronation as 1 June at Noyon with a second ceremony on 3 July in Paris; the traditional date is 3 July 987 at Noyon.

events.label: Co-coronation of son Robert as co-king
events.labelCn: 为儿子罗贝尔举行共治国王加冕
events.note: Robert was crowned co-king at Orléans on 25 December 987 (some accounts give 30 December).

events.label: Capture of rival Charles of Lorraine
events.labelCn: 俘获王位竞争者洛林公爵夏尔
events.note: Charles of Lower Lorraine, claimant to the throne since 987, was seized at Laon by Bishop Adalberon and handed to Hugh; imprisoned at Orléans.

events.label: Conspiracy of Adalberon of Laon and Odo I of Blois
events.labelCn: 拉昂主教阿达尔贝龙与布卢瓦伯爵厄德一世的密谋
events.note: A plot to deliver Hugh Capet into the custody of Emperor Otto III; it failed and went unpunished.

events.label: Patron of monastic reform
events.labelCn: 赞助修道院改革
events.note: Supported the Cluniac reform movement and monasteries such as Cluny, Fleury and Saint-Denis.

events.label: Death of Hugh Capet
events.labelCn: 于格·卡佩去世
events.note: Died at Les Juifs, near Prasville; interred at the Basilica of Saint-Denis.

deathCause.summary: Died 24 October 996 at Les Juifs, near Prasville (some accounts say Paris).
deathCause.detail: Wikipedia records no cause of death; later accounts sometimes attribute it to smallpox. Buried at the Basilica of Saint-Denis.
deathCause.summaryCn: 996年10月24日卒于莱瑞夫（普拉斯维尔附近），也有记载称卒于巴黎。
deathCause.detailCn: 维基百科未载死因，后世个别记载称其死于天花。葬于圣但尼圣殿。

sourceNote: Founder of the Capetian dynasty; the direct line here follows the father-to-son succession to Louis VII.
notes: Elected King of the Franks in 987; ancestor of the French royal line represented by Louis VII. Founder of the House of Capet, which ruled France (in direct and cadet lines) until 1848. Birth is commonly dated c. 939-941 (birthYear field holds 941). His father Hugh the Great is in the roster; his mother Hedwige of Saxony and wife Adelaide of Aquitaine are not.
fullNameCn: 法兰克人国王雨果·卡佩

fullName: Robert II, King of the Franks

events.label: Co-coronation as co-king at Orléans
events.labelCn: 在奥尔良加冕为共治国王
events.note: Crowned by the Archbishop of Reims at Sainte-Croix Cathedral, Orléans; some accounts give 30 December.

events.label: Became sole king on the death of Hugh Capet
events.labelCn: 于格·卡佩去世后继位为唯一国王

events.label: Marriage to Bertha of Burgundy
events.labelCn: 与勃艮第的贝尔塔成婚
events.note: Married in November/December 996; councils at Pavia (997) and Rome (998) condemned the consanguineous union; the couple separated in September 1001.

events.label: Annulment of marriage to Bertha
events.labelCn: 与贝尔塔的婚姻被废除
events.note: Marriage annulled in 1001 for consanguinity; Wikipedia notes the pope never actually promulgated the threatened excommunication.

events.label: Marriage to Constance of Arles
events.labelCn: 与阿尔勒的康斯坦丝成婚
events.note: Marriage contracted after October 1002 and before August 1004; conventionally dated 1003.

events.label: Burgundian succession war
events.labelCn: 勃艮第继承战争
events.note: After Duke Henry I of Burgundy died in 1002, Robert campaigned in Burgundy (siege of Beaune 1004; Avallon and Auxerre 1005); Otto-William renounced the duchy by the agreements of 1005-1006.

events.label: Revolt of sons Henry and Robert
events.labelCn: 儿子亨利与罗贝尔的叛乱
events.note: Around 1030 his sons Henry and Robert revolted, most likely intriguing with their mother Constance.

events.label: Death of Robert II
events.labelCn: 罗贝尔二世去世
events.note: Died at his residence in Melun of an overwhelming fever; buried at the Basilica of Saint-Denis.

deathCause.summary: Died 20 July 1031 at Melun of an overwhelming fever.
deathCause.detail: Died at his residence in Melun; buried at the Basilica of Saint-Denis.
deathCause.detailCn: 卒于默伦的居所，葬于圣但尼圣殿。

sourceNote: Son and successor of Hugh Capet; father of Henry I of France.
notes: Known as Robert the Pious; his reign continued the early Capetian succession. Son of Hugh Capet and Adelaide of Aquitaine. His three marriages (Rozala of Italy, Bertha of Burgundy, Constance of Arles) all involved consanguinity disputes; the annulment of the Bertha marriage was an early clash between the Capetian crown and the papacy. Exact birth year uncertain (c. 972).
fullNameCn: 法兰克人国王罗贝尔二世

fullName: Henri I, King of the Franks
deathPlaceCn: 维特里欧洛日，法兰西王国

events.label: Became Duke of Burgundy
events.labelCn: 受封勃艮第公爵
events.note: Received the duchy of Burgundy from his father Robert II in 1016; held it until 1032.

events.label: Coronation as co-king at Reims
events.labelCn: 在兰斯加冕为共治国王
events.note: Crowned co-king at Reims on 14 May 1027 while his father still lived.

events.label: Accession as King of the Franks
events.labelCn: 即位为法兰克人国王
events.note: Succeeded his father on 20 July 1031; his mother Constance supported his younger brother Robert as a rival candidate.

events.label: Settlement with brother Robert: grant of Burgundy
events.labelCn: 将勃艮第让予弟弟罗贝尔以平息争端
events.note: Gave the Duchy of Burgundy to his brother Robert as an appanage in 1032; the peace is sometimes dated 1034.

events.label: Marriage to Anne of Kiev
events.labelCn: 与基辅的安娜成婚
events.note: Traditional date 19 May 1051; some modern scholars argue for an earlier marriage, c. 1043-1049 — year uncertain.

events.label: Battle of Mortemer
events.labelCn: 莫尔特默战役
events.note: Invaded Normandy but was defeated by William (the future Conqueror).

events.label: Battle of Varaville
events.labelCn: 瓦拉维尔战役
events.note: Second defeat in Normandy; William caught Henry's army crossing the river Dives.

events.label: Death of Henry I
events.labelCn: 亨利一世去世
events.note: Died at Vitry-aux-Loges (the Wikipedia article text says Vitry-en-Brie) while besieging Thimert; buried at the Basilica of Saint-Denis.

deathCause.summary: Died 4 August 1060 at Vitry-aux-Loges while besieging Thimert.
deathCause.detail: Cause of death not recorded; Wikipedia infobox gives Vitry-aux-Loges, article text gives Vitry-en-Brie. Buried at the Basilica of Saint-Denis.
deathCause.summaryCn: 1060年8月4日围攻蒂梅尔时卒于维特里欧洛日。
deathCause.detailCn: 死因未见记载；维基百科信息框写作维特里欧洛日，正文写作维特里昂布里。葬于圣但尼圣殿。

sourceNote: Son of Robert II and father of Philip I of France.
notes: The French form Henri is used for the Capetian canonical display name; Henry I remains an English alias. His marriage to Anne of Kiev (traditional date 19 May 1051; earlier dating argued by some scholars) brought a princess of the Rurikid house of Kievan Rus' to France; she was the mother of Philippe I and acted as regent after Henri's death. His reign saw two failed invasions of Normandy (Mortemer 1054, Varaville 1057) against the rising William of Normandy.
fullNameCn: 法兰克人国王亨利一世

fullName: Philippe I, King of the Franks

events.label: Co-coronation at Reims
events.labelCn: 在兰斯加冕为共治国王
events.note: Crowned co-king at Reims on 23 May 1059 at about age seven.

events.label: Accession; regency of Anne of Kiev and Baldwin V of Flanders
events.labelCn: 即位；基辅的安娜与佛兰德的鲍德温五世摄政
events.note: Became king on 4 August 1060; his mother Anne of Kiev and Baldwin V of Flanders acted as regents until about 1067.

events.label: Battle of Cassel
events.labelCn: 卡塞尔战役
events.note: Intervened in the Flemish succession supporting Richilda of Flanders and was defeated by Robert the Frisian.

events.label: Marriage to Bertha of Holland
events.labelCn: 与荷兰的贝尔塔成婚
events.note: Bertha, mother of Louis VI, was repudiated in 1092.

events.label: Marriage to Bertrade de Montfort
events.labelCn: 与蒙福尔的贝特蕾德成婚
events.note: Repudiated Bertha of Holland (allegedly claiming she was too fat) and married Bertrade on 15 May 1092 while she was still married to Fulk IV of Anjou; led to conflict with the Church.

events.label: Excommunication by Pope Urban II
events.labelCn: 被教皇乌尔班二世处以绝罚
events.note: First banned by Hugh of Die in 1094; the sentence was renewed at the Council of Clermont (November 1095); Philip was absolved after a public penance in 1104.

events.label: Absent from the First Crusade
events.labelCn: 未参加第一次十字军东征
events.note: Philip did not take the cross, unlike his brother Hugh of Vermandois who was a major participant; troops from his demesne did join the crusade.

events.label: Death of Philip I
events.labelCn: 腓力一世去世
events.note: Died at the castle of Melun; buried at Fleury Abbey, Saint-Benoît-sur-Loire, at his own request, rather than at Saint-Denis.

deathCause.summary: Died 29 July 1108 at the castle of Melun.
deathCause.detail: Abbot Suger records that the king 'daily grew feebler'; no specific cause is given. Buried at Fleury Abbey (Saint-Benoît-sur-Loire) at his own request, not at Saint-Denis.
deathCause.detailCn: 叙热修道院长记载国王“日渐衰弱”，无具体死因。按本人遗愿葬于弗勒里修道院（圣伯努瓦-卢瓦尔），而非圣但尼。

sourceNote: Son of Henry I and father of Louis VI of France.
notes: The French form Philippe is used for the canonical display name; Philip I remains an English alias. His marriage to Bertrade de Montfort led to excommunication and a long conflict with the Church; he was the first Capetian king not buried at Saint-Denis. He did not take part in the First Crusade, and his reign saw the gradual encroachment of Norman (Anglo-Norman) power in the Vexin and elsewhere.
fullNameCn: 法兰克人国王腓力一世

fullName: Louis VI, King of the Franks
deathPlaceCn: 贝蒂西-圣皮埃尔，法兰西王国

events.label: Accession and coronation at Orléans
events.labelCn: 即位并在奥尔良加冕
events.note: Became king on 29 July 1108 and was crowned at Orléans on 3 August by Daimbert of Sens, as his half-brother blocked the route to Reims.

events.label: Wars against robber barons and royal-domain consolidation
events.labelCn: 讨伐盗匪贵族、巩固王室领地
events.note: Campaigns against Hugh of Crécy, Aymon Vaire-Vache and repeated sieges of Hugh of Le Puiset (1111-1113); Louis often led in person.

events.label: Marriage to Adélaide de Maurienne
events.labelCn: 与莫里耶讷的阿代拉伊德成婚
events.note: Married Adelaide, daughter of Humbert II of Savoy, on 3 August 1115; mother of his eight children.

events.label: Battle of Brémule
events.labelCn: 布雷米勒战役
events.note: Backing William Clito's claims in the war with Henry I of England over Gisors and Normandy, Louis's troops were routed at Brémule.

events.label: Imperial invasion of Henry V repelled at Reims
events.labelCn: 在兰斯挫败神圣罗马皇帝亨利五世的入侵
events.note: Henry V of Germany assembled an army to march on Reims, but the invasion was abandoned after the French nobility rallied behind Louis.

events.label: Intervention in Flanders
events.labelCn: 干预佛兰德事务
events.note: After the murder of Charles the Good (2 March 1127), Louis took Ghent, Bruges and Ypres and backed William Clito as Count; after Clito's death in 1128 Louis confirmed Thierry of Alsace.

events.label: Arranged marriage of Louis VII and Eleanor of Aquitaine
events.labelCn: 促成路易七世与阿基坦的埃莉诺的联姻
events.note: Named guardian of Eleanor by the dying William X of Aquitaine; the wedding took place at the cathedral of Saint-André in Bordeaux on 25 July 1137.

events.label: Death of Louis VI
events.labelCn: 路易六世去世
events.note: Died of dysentery at Béthisy-Saint-Pierre seven days after the wedding; buried at the Basilica of Saint-Denis.

deathCause.summary: Died 1 August 1137 at Béthisy-Saint-Pierre of dysentery.
deathCause.detail: Died seven days after the wedding of Louis VII and Eleanor of Aquitaine, which he had arranged; buried at the Basilica of Saint-Denis.
deathCause.summaryCn: 1137年8月1日因痢疾卒于贝蒂西-圣皮埃尔。
deathCause.detailCn: 在其促成路易七世与埃莉诺的婚礼七天后去世；葬于圣但尼圣殿。

sourceNote: Son of Philip I and father of Louis VII of France.
notes: The existing Louis VII card now links to Louis VI through fatherId. The first strong Capetian king: he consolidated the royal domain around Paris and Orléans, fought the robber barons, and relied on his chronicler and adviser Abbot Suger of Saint-Denis. His arranged marriage of Louis VII to Eleanor of Aquitaine brought the duchy of Aquitaine into the royal domain in 1137.
fullNameCn: 法兰克人国王路易六世

fullName: Philippe II Augustus, King of France

events.label: Coronation at Reims as co-king
events.labelCn: 在兰斯加冕为共治国王
events.note: Crowned at Reims on 1 November 1179 while his father Louis VII was in declining health.

events.label: Marriage to Isabella of Hainaut
events.labelCn: 与埃诺的伊莎贝拉结婚
events.note: Married at Bapaume on 28 April 1180; she brought Artois as her dowry and died in 1190.

events.label: Accession as sole King of France
events.labelCn: 成为法兰西唯一国王
events.note: Louis VII died 18 September 1180; Philip's sole reign ran 1180–1223.

events.label: Birth of heir Louis VIII
events.labelCn: 王储路易八世诞生
events.note: Son and future successor Louis VIII was born 5 September 1187.

events.label: Joined the Third Crusade
events.labelCn: 参加第三次十字军东征
events.note: Left Vézelay 4 July 1190, reached Acre in April 1191, and returned to France on 31 July 1191 after a dispute with Richard I.

events.label: Marriage to Ingeborg of Denmark
events.labelCn: 与丹麦的英格堡结婚
events.note: Married at Amiens on 14 August 1193; Philip repudiated her the same day and sought an annulment on grounds of non-consummation.

events.label: Repudiation of Ingeborg of Denmark
events.labelCn: 休弃英格堡
events.note: The annulment was refused by Popes Celestine III and Innocent III, leading to a long dispute that ended only with Ingeborg's restoration in 1213.

events.label: Marriage to Agnes of Meran
events.labelCn: 与梅兰的阿格尼丝结婚
events.note: Bigamous while Ingeborg was still alive; Innocent III declared the marriage null and placed France under interdict from 1199 until 7 September 1200. Agnes died in 1201.

events.label: Treaty of Le Goulet with King John
events.labelCn: 与约翰王签订《勒古莱条约》
events.note: May 1200; John acknowledged Philip's overlordship and paid a relief for his continental lands, easing the Ingeborg dispute with the papacy.

events.label: Conquest of Normandy
events.labelCn: 征服诺曼底
events.note: Château Gaillard fell in March 1204 after a five-month siege; by the end of 1204 most of Normandy and the Angevin lands were in Philip's hands.

events.label: Ingeborg restored as queen
events.labelCn: 迎回英格堡并恢复其王后地位
events.note: After Agnes's death Philip took Ingeborg back; she was recognised at court as queen from 1213.

events.label: Battle of Bouvines
events.labelCn: 布汶战役
events.note: 27 July 1214; Philip commanded the French royal army to a decisive victory over Emperor Otto IV and his coalition, securing his conquests.

events.label: Death at Mantes-la-Jolie
events.labelCn: 于芒特拉若利去世
events.note: Died 14 July 1223 of fever contracted while travelling in hot weather; buried at the Basilica of Saint-Denis.

sourceNote: First Capetian ruler to style himself King of France (Rex Franciae) from about 1190; the usage became established in royal documents by 1204. Marriage dates for Ingeborg follow the Wikipedia article (14 August 1193).
notes: The supreme-king visual tier is intentionally triggered by the King of France title. Crowned co-king in 1179; his reign roughly tripled the royal domain through the conquest of Normandy (1204) and the victory at Bouvines (1214).

deathCause.detail: Philip fell ill in September 1222, recovered, then succumbed to a fever while travelling in hot weather in the summer of 1223; he died on 14 July 1223 at Mantes-la-Jolie against his physicians' advice and was buried at Saint-Denis.
deathCause.detailCn: 腓力于 1222 年 9 月染病后康复，1223 年夏季因暑热旅途引发高烧，于 7 月 14 日在芒特拉若利去世，葬于圣但尼修道院。

fullNameCn: 法兰西国王腓力二世·奥古斯都

fullName: Adèle of Champagne, Queen of France
fullNameCn: 法兰西王后香槟的阿黛勒
sourceNote: Third wife of Louis VII and mother of Philip II Augustus.
notes: Added as Louis VII's default spouse; Eleanor of Aquitaine remains another spouse and can be selected with the spouse direction buttons. Daughter of Theobald II, Count of Champagne (birthplace Blois per Wikipedia infobox). Served as regent of France 1190-1191 with Archbishop William of the White Hands while Philip II was on the Third Crusade.

deathCause.detail: Adèle died in Paris on 4 June 1206, aged about 66; no violent cause is recorded. She was buried at Pontigny Abbey near Auxerre.
deathCause.detailCn: 阿黛勒于1206年6月4日在巴黎去世，享年约66岁；无暴力死因记载。葬于欧塞尔附近的蓬蒂尼修道院。

events.label: Marriage to Louis VII of France
events.labelCn: 与法兰西国王路易七世成婚
events.note: Married 13 November 1160, five weeks after the death of Louis's second wife Constance of Castile; the marriage sealed a peace with her father Count Theobald II.

events.label: Crowned Queen of France
events.labelCn: 加冕为法兰西王后
events.note: Crowned queen at Orléans on the day of her wedding, 13 November 1160.

events.label: Birth of Philip II Augustus
events.labelCn: 腓力二世·奥古斯都出生
events.note: Long-awaited son of Louis VII, born 21 August 1165 at Gonesse; nicknamed 'God-given' (Dieudonné).

events.label: Regent of France during the Third Crusade
events.labelCn: 第三次十字军东征期间摄政法兰西
events.note: Appointed regent by her son Philip II, acting together with Archbishop William of the White Hands from his departure in 1190 until his return in 1191.

events.label: Death of Adèle of Champagne
events.labelCn: 香槟的阿黛勒去世
events.note: Died 4 June 1206 in Paris; buried at Pontigny Abbey.

sourceNote: Daughter of Louis VII and Adèle of Champagne; married Alexios II Komnenos and later Andronikos I Komnenos according to the cited account.
notes: Her later Byzantine marital history is represented in source notes until spouse cards and cross-realm relationship records are added.
fullNameCn: 法兰西公主阿涅丝

fullName: Hugh the Great, Duke of the Franks

events.label: Count of Paris and Margrave of Neustria
events.labelCn: 成为巴黎伯爵与纽斯特里亚侯爵
events.note: Succeeded his father Robert I, who died at Soissons in 923; the exact dates are approximate.

events.label: Declined the Frankish crown
events.labelCn: 拒绝法兰克王位
events.note: After Robert I's death the crown passed to his brother-in-law Rudolph instead of Hugh.

events.label: Restored Louis IV from England
events.labelCn: 迎路易四世自英格兰归国为王
events.note: Took a very active part in bringing Louis IV (d'Outremer) back from the Kingdom of England in 936.

events.label: Duke of the Franks
events.labelCn: 受封法兰克公爵

events.label: Marriage to Hedwig of Saxony
events.labelCn: 与萨克森的哈德维希成婚
events.note: Daughter of Henry the Fowler; mother of his five children, including Hugh Capet.

events.label: Excommunicated at the Council of Ingelheim
events.labelCn: 在英格尔海姆会议上被处以绝罚
events.note: Excommunicated in absentia at the Council of Ingelheim over his conflicts with Louis IV.

events.label: Peace with Louis IV
events.labelCn: 与路易四世修和
events.note: Made peace with the king and the church.

events.label: Invested with Burgundy and Aquitaine
events.labelCn: 受封勃艮第与阿基坦
events.note: After Louis IV's death he backed Lothair's coronation and was invested with the two duchies; by April 956 he was master of Burgundy.

events.label: Death at Dourdan
events.labelCn: 在杜尔当去世
events.note: 16 or 17 June 956; buried at the Basilica of Saint-Denis.

deathCause.summary: Died of natural causes at Dourdan
deathCause.detail: Hugh died at Dourdan on 16 June (some sources say 17 June) 956, at the height of his power, about two months after becoming master of Burgundy. No violent or suspicious cause is recorded.
deathCause.detailCn: 956 年 6 月 16 日（一说 17 日）大于格在杜尔当去世，时值其权力巅峰，距其成为勃艮第实际主宰仅两个月左右。史料未载暴力或可疑死因。

sourceNote: Father of Hugh Capet; son of Robert I of France and Béatrice of Vermandois.
notes: The maternal link to Béatrice opens the documented Vermandois-Carolingian descent. Duke of the Franks and the most powerful magnate of West Francia; father of Hugh Capet, founder of the Capetian dynasty.
fullNameCn: 法兰克公爵大于格

displayNameCn: 韦尔芒杜瓦的贝阿特丽丝
fullNameCn: 韦尔芒杜瓦的贝阿特丽丝
sourceNote: Daughter of Herbert I of Vermandois and mother of Hugh the Great; wife of Robert I of France.
notes: Her descent from the Carolingian line is through her father. Married c. 890 as the second wife of Robert of Neustria (later King Robert I); ancestress of the Capetian dynasty through her son Hugh the Great. Died after 26 March 931.

deathCause.detail: Béatrice's last known attestation is 26 March 931; she died after that date, but the exact year, place and circumstances are not documented.
deathCause.detailCn: 贝阿特丽丝最后一次见于记载是931年3月26日；她在此之后去世，但确切年份、地点与情形均无记载。

events.label: Birth of Béatrice of Vermandois (c. 880)
events.labelCn: 韦尔芒杜瓦的贝阿特丽丝出生（约880年）
events.note: Born c. 880; exact date and place unknown.

events.label: Marriage to Robert of Neustria
events.labelCn: 与纽斯特里亚的罗贝尔成婚
events.note: Married c. 890 as the second wife of Robert of Neustria, who later reigned as King Robert I of France (922-923).

events.label: Became Queen of the Franks
events.labelCn: 成为法兰克王后
events.note: Robert was elected king in 922; Béatrice was queen consort 922-923.

events.label: Robert I killed at the Battle of Soissons
events.labelCn: 罗贝尔一世在苏瓦松之战中阵亡
events.note: Her husband was killed on 15 June 923; their son Hugh the Great was offered the crown but refused. Béatrice was left a widow.

events.label: Death of Béatrice of Vermandois (after 931)
events.labelCn: 韦尔芒杜瓦的贝阿特丽丝去世（931年之后）
events.note: Last attested 26 March 931; died after that date, exact date unknown.

displayNameCn: 韦尔芒杜瓦的赫伯特一世
fullNameCn: 韦尔芒杜瓦伯爵赫伯特一世
sourceNote: Son of Pepin of Vermandois and father of Béatrice of Vermandois.
notes: Carolingian male-line descendant through Pepin of Italy. Count of Vermandois and Soissons; his dates of accession vary by source (text: before 889; infobox: 893; existing record: 896). His capture and murder of his brother Raoul in 896 may have led Baldwin II of Flanders to have him killed in 907 (speculative).

deathCause.summary: Possibly assassinated on Baldwin II's orders
deathCause.detail: Herbert died in 907. Some historians speculate that Baldwin II of Flanders had him assassinated, possibly in retaliation for Herbert's capture and murder of his own brother Raoul in 896; the accounts are uncertain, and no battle or natural cause is recorded.
deathCause.detailCn: 赫伯特于907年去世。有史家推测他是被佛兰德伯爵鲍德温二世派人暗杀的，可能与896年赫伯特俘杀亲兄弟拉乌尔一事有关；此说尚不确定，史料亦未记载战斗或自然死亡。

events.label: Birth of Herbert I (c. 848)
events.labelCn: 赫伯特一世出生（约848年）
events.note: Born c. 848/850; exact date unknown.

events.label: Became Count of Vermandois and Soissons
events.labelCn: 成为韦尔芒杜瓦与苏瓦松伯爵
events.note: Accession date uncertain: Wikipedia text says before 889, the infobox gives 893, the existing record uses 896.

events.label: Capture and murder of his brother Raoul
events.labelCn: 俘杀其兄弟拉乌尔
events.note: Herbert captured his brother Raoul in the upper Somme valley and had him murdered rather than ransomed; some historians link this to his own later death.

events.label: Death of Herbert I
events.labelCn: 赫伯特一世去世
events.note: Died 907; possibly assassinated on the orders of Baldwin II of Flanders (speculative).

fullNameCn: 韦尔芒杜瓦伯爵丕平
sourceNote: Son of Bernard of Italy and ancestor of the Vermandois branch.
notes: Often styled Pepin I of Vermandois in genealogical references. Son of Bernard of Italy and great-grandson of Charlemagne; held Vermandois, Senlis, Péronne and Saint-Quentin. NOTE: this is Pepin I, who died c. 850 (after 850 in some genealogies) — not Pepin II (d. c. 893) nor the 'after 922' figure. Death year corrected from 845 to c. 850 per Wikipedia.

deathCause.detail: Pepin died c. 850 (some genealogies say after 850). No violent or suspicious circumstances are recorded; the exact date and cause are not documented.
deathCause.detailCn: 丕平约于850年去世（部分谱系记载为850年之后）。史料未记载暴力或可疑的情形，确切日期与死因均无记载。

events.label: Birth of Pepin of Vermandois (c. 815)
events.labelCn: 韦尔芒杜瓦的丕平出生（约815年）
events.note: Born c. 815 (Wikipedia infobox: c. 817); exact date unknown.

events.label: Count of Vermandois, Senlis, Péronne and Saint-Quentin
events.labelCn: 任韦尔芒杜瓦、桑利、佩罗讷与圣康坦伯爵
events.note: Date of succession uncertain; Wikipedia notes his son Pepin II held the county from 850.

events.label: Supported Emperor Lothar after Louis the Pious's death
events.labelCn: 虔诚者路易去世后支持皇帝洛泰尔
events.note: Despite earlier allegiance to Charles the Bald, Pepin supported Emperor Lothar in the succession struggle after Louis the Pious died (840).

events.label: Death of Pepin of Vermandois
events.labelCn: 韦尔芒杜瓦的丕平去世
events.note: Died c. 850 (some sources: after 850); exact date unknown.

events.label: King of Italy
events.labelCn: 成为意大利国王
events.note: Succeeded his father Pepin; Charlemagne confirmed him in 812 and 813.

events.label: Rebellion against Louis the Pious
events.labelCn: 起兵反抗虔诚者路易
events.note: After the Ordinatio Imperii made him a vassal of his cousin Lothair; he surrendered at Chalon and was taken to Aachen.

events.label: Condemned for treason; blinded
events.labelCn: 以叛国罪被定罪并遭刺瞎双眼
events.note: Tried and condemned for treason at the end of 817; the death sentence was commuted to blinding with a red-hot stiletto.

events.label: Death from blinding wounds at Aachen
events.labelCn: 在亚琛因失明酷刑去世
events.note: Died in agony two days after the blinding procedure; buried at Milan.

deathCause.summary: Blinded on Louis the Pious's orders; died of the wounds
deathCause.detail: After his 817 rebellion Bernard was tried for treason and sentenced to death, commuted to blinding, carried out by pressing a red-hot stiletto to the eyeballs. He died in agony two days later, on 17 April 818 at Aachen. The blinding was punishment for rebellion against Louis the Pious.
deathCause.summaryCn: 被刺瞎双眼后伤重而死
deathCause.detailCn: 817 年叛乱失败后，伯纳德以叛国罪受审，死刑被改为刺瞎双眼（以烧红的利器灼烧眼球）。两天后即 818 年 4 月 17 日，他在亚琛痛苦死去。失明是对其背叛虔诚者路易的惩罚。

sourceNote: Son of Pepin of Italy and grandson of Charlemagne.
notes: His son Pepin founded the Vermandois branch. An illegitimate son of Pepin of Italy, born c. 797 in Vermandois. Death place is Aachen (Milan is his burial place). His 817 plot against Louis the Pious ended his life; the Carolingian male line descended through him to the counts of Vermandois.
fullNameCn: 意大利国王伯纳德

events.label: Birth as Carloman; renamed Pepin at baptism
events.labelCn: 出生（本名卡洛曼）
events.note: Born 777 to Charlemagne and Hildegard (alternative c. 773); renamed Pepin at his baptism in 781.

events.label: Crowned King of the Lombards by Pope Adrian I
events.labelCn: 教皇阿德里安一世为其加冕为伦巴第国王
events.note: Crowned in Rome at the age of four; later styled King of Italy, ruling under Charlemagne-appointed advisors with his court based at Verona.

events.label: Campaign in Bavaria
events.labelCn: 出征巴伐利亚

events.label: Avar campaign; destruction of the Avar Khaganate
events.labelCn: 远征阿瓦尔，摧毁阿瓦尔汗国
events.note: Led the campaign that took the Avar stronghold and precipitated the collapse of the Avar state.

events.label: Birth of son Bernard (future King of Italy)
events.labelCn: 儿子伯纳德（未来的意大利国王）出生
events.note: c. 797; Bernard later rebelled and died after being blinded in 818.

events.label: Campaign against Venice
events.labelCn: 征讨威尼斯

events.label: Death at Milan
events.labelCn: 在米兰去世
events.note: Died 8 July 810, predeceasing Charlemagne; Milan is the traditional death place, and the deaths of several family members in 810-811 may relate to an epidemic.

deathCause.detail: Pepin died on 8 July 810, before his father Charlemagne. The traditional death place is Milan; several Carolingian family deaths in 810-811 may have been caused by an epidemic spread from cattle. No violent cause is recorded.
deathCause.detailCn: 810 年 7 月 8 日，丕平先于其父查理曼去世。传统说法称其殁于米兰；810—811 年间加洛林家族多名成员相继去世，可能与由牲畜传播的疫情有关。史料未载暴力死因。

sourceNote: Son of Charlemagne and father of Bernard of Italy.
notes: The direct Carolingian bridge into the Vermandois line. Born 777 (alternative c. 773); baptized in 781 and renamed Pepin from Carloman. His male-line descendants (counts of Vermandois) outlasted all other Carolingian male lines.
fullNameCn: 意大利国王丕平

events.label: Became King of the Franks
events.labelCn: 成为法兰克国王
events.note: Crowned jointly with his brother Carloman I at separate coronations in Noyon and Soissons.

events.label: Sole king of the Franks
events.labelCn: 成为法兰克唯一国王
events.note: Became sole ruler after Carloman died suddenly on 4 December 771.

events.label: Marriage to Hildegard
events.labelCn: 与希尔迪加德成婚
events.note: Married Hildegard in 771 after setting aside his brief marriage to Desiderius's daughter; she bore most of his surviving heirs and died in 783.

events.label: Saxon Wars begin
events.labelCn: 萨克森战争开始
events.note: Over 30 years of nearly continuous warfare (772-804) to subdue and convert the Saxons; began with the destruction of the Irminsul.

events.label: Conquest of the Lombard kingdom
events.labelCn: 征服伦巴第王国
events.note: Siege of Pavia from late 773; the city surrendered by June 774 and Desiderius was deposed.

events.label: Became King of the Lombards
events.labelCn: 成为伦巴第国王

events.label: Battle of Roncevaux Pass
events.labelCn: 龙塞斯瓦耶斯战役
events.note: Defeat of the Frankish rearguard by Basques in the Pyrenees while returning from Spain; traditionally dated 15 August 778. (The later Roland legend is not treated as history here.)

events.label: Massacre of Verden
events.labelCn: 凡尔登大屠杀
events.note: Allegedly 4,500 Saxon prisoners executed in 782 after a Saxon revolt; not a conventional battle, and the numbers are debated.

events.label: Submission and baptism of Widukind
events.labelCn: 维杜金德归顺受洗
events.note: By 785 the Saxon leader Widukind agreed to be baptised, with Charlemagne as his godfather.

events.label: Conquest of the Avars
events.labelCn: 征服阿瓦尔人
events.note: After campaigns in 788-796, including Pepin of Italy's later wars, the Avar kingdom collapsed and its treasure was brought to Aachen.

events.label: Imperial coronation in Rome
events.labelCn: 罗马加冕称帝
events.note: Crowned 'Emperor of the Romans' by Pope Leo III at St Peter's on Christmas Day 800; Einhard claims Charlemagne said he would not have entered the church had he known of the plan.

events.label: Imperial reforms and Carolingian Renaissance
events.labelCn: 帝国改革与加洛林文艺复兴
events.note: The 802 Capitulary of Aachen revised the laws, and the court school under Alcuin fostered a cultural revival across the empire.

events.label: Louis the Pious crowned co-emperor
events.labelCn: 路易一世加冕为共治皇帝
events.note: In 813 Charlemagne crowned his son Louis co-emperor at Aachen, securing the succession within the family.

events.label: Death of Charlemagne
events.labelCn: 查理曼去世
events.note: Died on 28 January 814 at Aachen after an illness (Einhard reports pleurisy); buried in the Palatine Chapel.

sourceNote: King of the Franks and emperor; father of Pepin of Italy.
notes: The Carolingian ancestor anchoring the Vermandois-to-Capetian line. Birth year disputed: 742 (traditional) vs 747/748 (preferred by current scholarship and the Wikipedia article); birth place traditionally Herstal but uncertain. Mother Bertrada of Laon and the wives Hildegard/Fastrada/Luitgard are not in the roster; the roster's 'Hildegard' entry is kept as a child (an infant daughter of that name existed, as did the queen of the same name).

deathCause.detail: Charlemagne died on 28 January 814 at Aachen, traditionally attributed to illness (Einhard reports pleurisy) after declining health in his final years.
deathCause.detailCn: 查理曼于 814 年 1 月 28 日在亚琛去世，传统上认为死于疾病（艾因哈德记载为胸膜炎），此前晚年健康已每况愈下。

fullNameCn: 罗马人的皇帝查理曼
birthPlaceCn: 法兰克王国赫斯塔尔（今比利时）
deathPlaceCn: 法兰克王国亚琛（今德国）

fullName: Pepin the Short, King of the Franks

events.label: Co-Mayor of the Palace with Carloman
events.labelCn: 与卡洛曼共任宫相
events.note: After Charles Martel's death; Pepin took Neustria while Carloman took Austrasia.

events.label: Sole Mayor of the Palace
events.labelCn: 独任宫相
events.note: Carloman retired to a monastery, leaving Pepin sole mayor and dux et princeps Francorum.

events.label: Deposed Childeric III; elected King of the Franks
events.labelCn: 废黜希尔德里克三世，当选法兰克国王
events.note: The last Merovingian king was deposed and confined to a monastery after Pope Zachary's ruling.

events.label: Anointed King at Soissons
events.labelCn: 在苏瓦松受膏加冕
events.note: No exact date is recorded; tradition gives November 751.

events.label: Re-anointed by Pope Stephen II at Saint-Denis
events.labelCn: 教皇斯德望二世在圣但尼为其再行加冕
events.note: Midsummer 754; his sons Charles and Carloman were anointed too and made Patricians of Rome.

events.label: Donation of Pepin
events.labelCn: 丕平献土
events.note: Year commonly given as 756, after the second Lombard campaign; the donation established the Papal States.

events.label: Second Italian campaign against Aistulf
events.labelCn: 再征意大利讨伐艾斯图夫
events.note: Standard accounts date the two Lombard campaigns to 754 and 756; the second forced Aistulf to cede territory to the papacy.

events.label: Death at Saint-Denis
events.labelCn: 在圣但尼去世
events.note: One account says he died on campaign; he was buried in the Basilica of Saint-Denis.

deathCause.detail: Pepin died on 24 September 768, aged 53-54. Sources record no violence or suspicious circumstances; he was buried in the Basilica of Saint-Denis.
deathCause.detailCn: 768 年 9 月 24 日，矮子丕平去世，享年约 54 岁。史料未记载暴力或可疑死因；他安葬于圣但尼圣殿。

sourceNote: Founder of the Carolingian royal line; father of Charlemagne.
notes: The direct predecessor of Charlemagne in the project chain. Birth year c. 714 is approximate; birthplace Jupille is traditional. He ended the Merovingian line and, with the papal alliance (754, 756), legitimated the Carolingian kingship.
fullNameCn: 法兰克国王矮子丕平

fullName: Charles Martel, Mayor of the Palace
deathPlaceCn: 法兰克瓦兹河畔基耶尔济

titles.title: Duke and Prince of the Franks

events.label: Acclaimed Mayor of the Palace of Austrasia
events.labelCn: 被拥立为奥斯特拉西亚宫相
events.note: Escaped imprisonment by Plectrude after the death of Pepin of Herstal; the exact year is 715 or 716.

events.label: Battle of Amblève
events.labelCn: 安布勒沃战役
events.note: His first major victory after escaping prison; the turning point of the Frankish civil war.

events.label: Battle of Soissons; recognized over all Frankish kingdoms
events.labelCn: 苏瓦松战役，确立对法兰克诸国的统治
events.note: Defeated the alliance of Chilperic II and Odo the Great, winning recognition of his mayoralty over all the Frankish kingdoms.

events.label: Battle of Tours (Poitiers)
events.labelCn: 图尔战役（普瓦捷战役）
events.note: Defeated the Umayyad army of Abd al-Rahman al-Ghafiqi. The exact day is unknown; tradition dates it to October 732.

events.label: Battle of the Boarn; subjugation of Frisia
events.labelCn: 博尔恩河战役，征服弗里西亚
events.note: Slain the Frisian duke Bubo and subjugated Frisia.

events.label: Campaign in Provence and Septimania
events.labelCn: 远征普罗旺斯与塞普提马尼亚
events.note: Sieges of Avignon, Narbonne and Nîmes against the Umayyads.

events.label: Ruled the Franks without a king
events.labelCn: 无王在位期间统治法兰克
events.note: After King Theuderic IV died no successor was appointed; the throne stayed vacant until Charles's death in 741.

events.label: Divided the realm among his sons
events.labelCn: 将国土分封给诸子
events.note: c. 740; Carloman, Pepin the Short and Grifo received shares.

events.label: Death at Quierzy
events.labelCn: 在基耶尔济去世

deathCause.summary: Died of natural causes at Quierzy
deathCause.detail: Charles Martel died on 22 October 741 at Quierzy-sur-Oise. Sources record no violence or unusual illness; he was buried at the Basilica of Saint-Denis.
deathCause.detailCn: 741 年 10 月 22 日，查理·马特在瓦兹河畔基耶尔济去世。史料未记载暴力或异常病因；他安葬于圣但尼圣殿。

sourceNote: Carolingian ruler and father of Pepin the Short; victor of the Battle of Tours.
notes: The requested upper endpoint of the early medieval chain. Birth year is usually given as c. 688 (other estimates 676-690). He wielded royal power as Mayor of the Palace and Duke and Prince of the Franks without taking the royal title.
fullNameCn: 宫相查理·马特

sourceNote: Father of Alfred the Great and four elder sons who ruled Wessex before him; birth year not recorded (c. 795 is an estimate) and the 838/839 dating of his accession is debated.
notes: First son to succeed his father as West Saxon king since 641; husband of Osburh, then of Judith of Flanders.

deathCause.summary: Died of natural causes, no illness recorded
deathCause.detail: Æthelwulf died on 13 January 858 in his early sixties; no cause is recorded, and his death is presumed natural. He was buried first at Steyning (Sussex) and later transferred to Winchester, probably by Alfred.
deathCause.detailCn: 858 年 1 月 13 日埃塞尔伍尔夫在六十岁上下去世；无死因记载，推测为自然死亡。初葬于斯泰宁（萨塞克斯），后（可能由阿尔弗雷德）迁葬温彻斯特。

events.label: Became sub-king of Kent, Surrey, Sussex and Essex
events.labelCn: 成为肯特、萨里、萨塞克斯与埃塞克斯副王
events.note: Sent with an army to Kent in 825 by his father Ecgberht; expelled the sub-king Baldred and was appointed sub-king of the south-east.

events.label: Succeeded Ecgberht as King of Wessex
events.labelCn: 继承埃格伯特成为威塞克斯国王
events.note: First father-son succession in Wessex since 641; he may have been consecrated king at Kingston in 838, and is possibly styled rex Saxonum in a charter of that year.

events.label: Defeated by Vikings at Carhampton
events.labelCn: 在卡汉普顿被维京人击败
events.note: A Viking fleet and army fought Æthelwulf at Carhampton, Somerset; the West Saxons were defeated in 843.

events.label: Battle of Aclea: great victory over the Vikings
events.labelCn: 阿克利亚战役：大胜维京人
events.note: The Anglo-Saxon Chronicle calls it 'the greatest slaughter of a heathen army that we have ever heard of up to the present day'.

events.label: Daughter Æthelswith married Burgred, King of Mercia
events.labelCn: 女儿埃塞尔维斯嫁给麦西亚国王伯格雷德
events.note: Æthelwulf also joined the Mercian expedition into Wales in the same year.

events.label: Pilgrimage to Rome with his son Alfred
events.labelCn: 与幼子阿尔弗雷德赴罗马朝圣
events.note: Left in spring 855 and stayed in Rome a year, giving lavish gifts including a gold crown weighing 4 pounds; before leaving he granted a 'decimation', donating a tenth of his lands.

events.label: Married Judith, daughter of Charles the Bald
events.labelCn: 迎娶秃头查理之女朱迪丝
events.note: Married on 1 October 856 at Verberie and anointed by Hincmar, Archbishop of Rheims; Judith was aged 12 or 13.

events.label: Division of the kingdom after Æthelbald's revolt
events.labelCn: 埃塞尔博尔德叛乱后分割王国
events.note: On returning from Rome in October 856 he faced a revolt led by his son Æthelbald; the kingdom was divided to avoid civil war, either by Æthelbald keeping Wessex or the kingdom being split at Selwood Forest.

events.label: Died, buried first at Steyning then at Winchester
events.labelCn: 去世，初葬斯泰宁后迁温彻斯特
events.note: 13 January 858; succeeded by Æthelbald in Wessex and Æthelberht in Kent.

fullNameCn: 威塞克斯国王埃塞尔伍尔夫

sourceNote: Father of Æthelwulf and traditionally descended from the earlier West Saxon line; year of birth uncertain (born in the 770s) and the length of his exile in Francia (3 vs 13 years) is disputed.
notes: Grandfather of Alfred the Great; ended Mercian domination of southern England and was the eighth acknowledged bretwalda.

deathCause.summary: Natural death at an advanced age
deathCause.detail: Ecgberht died in 839 after a reign of 37 years, aged about seventy; no cause is recorded and his death is presumed natural. He was buried in Winchester.
deathCause.detailCn: 839 年埃格伯特在位 37 年后去世，享年约七十岁；无死因记载，推测为自然死亡。葬于温彻斯特。

events.label: Driven into exile in Francia by Offa and Beorhtric
events.labelCn: 被奥法与贝奥赫特里克放逐至法兰克
events.note: Probably exiled in 789 to the court of Charlemagne; the Anglo-Saxon Chronicle says three years, but many historians read it as thirteen (789-802).

events.label: Became King of Wessex
events.labelCn: 成为威塞克斯国王
events.note: On Beorhtric's death in 802 Ecgberht returned from exile and took the West Saxon throne.

events.label: Battle of Ellendun: defeated Beornwulf of Mercia
events.labelCn: 埃伦登战役：击败麦西亚国王伯恩伍尔夫
events.note: Fought at Wroughton near Swindon; the victory ended Mercian domination of southern England.

events.label: Conquest of Kent, Essex, Surrey and Sussex
events.labelCn: 征服肯特、埃塞克斯、萨里与萨塞克斯
events.note: 825-826; his son Æthelwulf drove Baldred, king of Kent, north over the Thames, and the south-eastern peoples submitted.

events.label: Conquered Mercia; Northumbrians submitted at Dore
events.labelCn: 征服麦西亚；诺森布里亚人在多尔归顺
events.note: Drove Wiglaf of Mercia into exile, ruled Mercia directly for a time, controlled the London mint and coined as King of Mercia; later in 829 the Northumbrians submitted to him at Dore.

events.label: Acknowledged as the eighth 'Wide-ruler' (bretwalda)
events.labelCn: 被承认为第八位不列颠统治者（bretwalda）
events.note: The Anglo-Saxon Chronicle lists him as the eighth king to hold the imperium over the other kingdoms of Britain.

events.label: Wiglaf recovered Mercia
events.labelCn: 维格拉夫夺回麦西亚
events.note: Wiglaf 'obtained the kingdom of Mercia again' in 830; Ecgberht nevertheless kept control of Kent, Essex and Surrey, and led a successful expedition against the Welsh in the same year.

events.label: Battle of Hingston Down; Council of Kingston
events.labelCn: 欣斯顿山战役；金斯顿会议
events.note: Defeated an alliance of Danes and West Welsh in Cornwall; at the Council of Kingston in 838 he and Æthelwulf secured church support for the succession.

events.label: Died; buried at Winchester
events.labelCn: 去世，葬于温彻斯特
events.note: Died in 839 after a 37-year reign; succeeded by his son Æthelwulf.

fullNameCn: 威塞克斯国王埃格伯特

sourceNote: Father of Ecgberht; his own parentage is disputed in the West Saxon genealogies, and his birth and death dates (c. 745 and c. 785) are unrecorded estimates — his reign is known only from a single charter of 784.
notes: Historical stopping point for the reliable Alfredian paternal line; only contemporary evidence of his kingship is charter S 38 of 784.

deathCause.summary: Fate unknown; probably killed or driven out in 785
deathCause.detail: No contemporary record survives of Ealhmund's death; he was probably killed or driven out when Offa of Mercia reasserted control of Kent in 785.
deathCause.summaryCn: 结局不明；785 年或被杀死或被驱逐
deathCause.detailCn: 埃尔蒙德之死无当代记载；785 年麦西亚国王奥法重夺肯特时，他或被杀死或被驱逐出位。

events.label: King of Kent, attested by a charter at Reculver
events.labelCn: 肯特国王，以雷库弗契约为证
events.note: The only contemporary evidence is charter S 38 of 784, granting land at Sheldwich to the abbot of Reculver with no reference to Offa of Mercia; his identification as Ecgberht's father rests on the West Saxon genealogies, which some historians consider fabricated.

events.label: Offa of Mercia regained Kent
events.labelCn: 麦西亚的奥法夺回肯特
events.note: By 785 Offa had regained control of Kent; Ealhmund was probably killed or driven out.

events.label: End of his reign; death date and circumstances unknown
events.labelCn: 统治终结，去世时间与情形不明
events.note: No death date survives; c. 785 is inferred from Offa's reconquest of Kent.

fullNameCn: 肯特国王埃尔蒙德

sourceNote: Elder son of Æthelwulf; often identified as Alfred's eldest brother.
notes: Basic sibling card; event timeline intentionally left empty.
fullNameCn: 威塞克斯的埃塞尔斯坦

sourceNote: Elder brother of Alfred and king of Wessex before him; year of birth unknown (c. 834 is an estimate) and the exact mechanics of the 856 division of the kingdom are disputed.
notes: Second son of Æthelwulf; his marriage to his widowed stepmother Judith was denounced by Asser but not opposed at the time; died childless.

deathCause.detail: Æthelbald died in 860, probably in about July, aged about 26; no cause is recorded — later writers speak only of a 'premature death'. He was buried at Sherborne Abbey, Dorset.
deathCause.detailCn: 860 年（约 7 月）埃塞尔博尔德去世，年仅约 26 岁；无死因记载，后世编年史仅称其早逝。葬于多塞特舍伯恩修道院。

events.label: Fought with his father at the Battle of Aclea
events.labelCn: 与父亲并肩参加阿克利亚战役
events.note: The Anglo-Saxon Chronicle records that Æthelwulf and Æthelbald defeated the Vikings at Aclea in 851, 'the greatest slaughter of a heathen army... before or since'.

events.label: Appointed King of Wessex while Æthelwulf went to Rome
events.labelCn: 在父亲赴罗马期间受封威塞克斯国王
events.note: Before leaving on pilgrimage in 855 Æthelwulf appointed Æthelbald king of Wessex and Æthelberht king of Kent.

events.label: Revolt against his father; the kingdom was divided
events.labelCn: 反叛其父，王国被分割
events.note: On Æthelwulf's return in October 856 with his bride Judith, Æthelbald refused to give up the crown; the kingdom was divided rather than risk civil war — either Æthelbald kept Wessex while Æthelberht yielded Kent, or Wessex itself was split at Selwood Forest.

events.label: Married his widowed stepmother Judith
events.labelCn: 迎娶寡居的继母朱迪丝
events.note: After Æthelwulf's death on 13 January 858; Asser denounced the union but it provoked no opposition at the time, and Judith attested his charters.

events.label: Died; buried at Sherborne Abbey
events.labelCn: 去世，葬于舍伯恩修道院
events.note: Died in 860, probably in about July; succeeded by his brother Æthelberht, who reunited Wessex and Kent.

fullNameCn: 威塞克斯国王埃塞尔博尔德

sourceNote: Brother of Alfred and king of Wessex before him; year of birth unknown (c. 835 is an estimate) and his death in autumn 865 is recorded only as of unknown causes.
notes: Third of five sons of Æthelwulf; the first king to rule Wessex and Kent as a fully united kingdom; died childless.

deathCause.detail: Æthelberht died of unknown causes in the autumn of 865 and was buried at Sherborne Abbey, Dorset, beside his brother Æthelbald.
deathCause.detailCn: 865 年秋埃塞尔伯特死因不明而去世，葬于多塞特舍伯恩修道院，与其兄埃塞尔博尔德为邻。

events.label: Appointed sub-king of Kent, Essex, Sussex and Surrey
events.labelCn: 受封肯特、埃塞克斯、萨塞克斯与萨里副王
events.note: Appointed by his father Æthelwulf in 855 when the king left for Rome; on Æthelwulf's death in 858 he ruled the south-east until 860.

events.label: Succeeded Æthelbald, reuniting Wessex and Kent
events.labelCn: 继承埃塞尔博尔德，重新统一威塞克斯与肯特
events.note: Æthelbald died childless in 860; Æthelberht appointed no sub-king, and Wessex and Kent were fully united for the first time.

events.label: Raid on Winchester repelled
events.labelCn: 击退对温彻斯特的袭击
events.note: A Viking army from the Somme sacked Winchester in 860 but was then defeated by the men of Hampshire and Berkshire; his reign 'began and ended with raids by the Vikings'.

events.label: Died in autumn 865 of unknown causes; buried at Sherborne
events.labelCn: 865 年秋去世，死因不明，葬于舍伯恩
events.note: Died childless in the autumn of 865 and was succeeded by his brother Æthelred I.

fullNameCn: 威塞克斯国王埃塞尔伯特

sourceNote: Brother of Alfred and king of Wessex immediately before him; born 845/848 (year disputed) and the precise circumstances of his death at Merton in April 871 are uncertain.
notes: Fourth of five sons of Æthelwulf; reigned during the first great Viking invasions of Wessex; father of Æthelhelm and Æthelwold.

deathCause.summary: Died at Merton in the Viking wars
deathCause.detail: Æthelred died at Merton (Meretun), Wessex, shortly after Easter 871 (15 April), weeks after the defeat at the Battle of Meretun on 22 March 871; tradition attributes his death to wounds received in the battle, though contemporary sources record no diagnosis. He was buried at Wimborne Minster.
deathCause.summaryCn: 维京战争期间卒于默顿
deathCause.detailCn: 871 年复活节（4 月 15 日）后不久，埃塞尔雷德一世卒于威塞克斯默顿（梅雷顿），距 3 月 22 日梅雷顿战役战败仅数周；传统认为其死于战役所受创伤，但当代史料未载具体情形。葬于温伯恩大教堂。

events.label: Succeeded his brother Æthelberht as King of Wessex
events.labelCn: 继承兄长埃塞尔伯特成为威塞克斯国王
events.note: In the same year the Viking Great Heathen Army landed in East Anglia, beginning the invasions that dominated his reign.

events.label: Campaign in Mercia against the Great Heathen Army
events.labelCn: 在麦西亚对抗维京大军的征战
events.note: Late 867; Æthelred and his brother Alfred led a West Saxon army to help King Burgred of Mercia relieve Nottingham, but the siege failed and Burgred paid off the Danes.

events.label: Battle of Ashdown: victory over the Vikings
events.labelCn: 阿什当战役：击败维京人
events.note: c. 8 January 871; the West Saxons won and the Viking king Bagsecg was killed; Alfred led the attack while Æthelred heard Mass, a detail Asser uses to Æthelred's disadvantage.

events.label: Battle of Meretun: defeat; he died shortly afterwards
events.labelCn: 梅雷顿战役：战败，旋即去世
events.note: 22 March 871; the West Saxons were defeated and Bishop Heahmund of Sherborne was killed; Æthelred died shortly after Easter (15 April), traditionally of wounds from this battle.

events.label: Died at Merton; buried at Wimborne Minster
events.labelCn: 卒于默顿，葬于温伯恩大教堂
events.note: Died late April 871 shortly after Easter; his young sons were passed over and his brother Alfred succeeded him.

fullNameCn: 威塞克斯国王埃塞尔雷德一世

sourceNote: Daughter of Alfred the Great and ruler of Mercia; birth year approximate (c. 870) and her marriage to Æthelred of Mercia can only be dated to the mid-880s.
notes: Eldest child of Alfred the Great; with her brother Edward the Elder she reconquered the southern Danelaw; mother of Ælfwynn.

deathCause.detail: Æthelflæd died at Tamworth on 12 June 918, 'eight days before midsummer' per the Anglo-Saxon Chronicle; no diagnosis is recorded, but her death is traditionally attributed to illness. She was buried beside her husband at St Oswald's Minster, Gloucester.
deathCause.detailCn: 据《盎格鲁-撒克逊编年史》，918 年 6 月 12 日（仲夏前八日）埃塞尔弗莱德卒于塔姆沃思；虽无病症记载，传统上认为死于疾病。葬于格洛斯特圣奥斯瓦尔德修道院，与丈夫合葬。

events.label: Married Æthelred, Lord of the Mercians
events.labelCn: 嫁给麦西亚领主埃塞尔雷德
events.note: Year approximate; Alfred sealed the alliance with Mercia in the mid-880s, and she is first recorded as Æthelred's wife in a charter of 887.

events.label: Raid on the northern Danelaw; relics of St Oswald taken to Gloucester
events.labelCn: 袭击北方丹麦法区；圣奥斯瓦尔德遗骸迁至格洛斯特
events.note: A West Saxon and Mercian force raided the northern Danelaw in 909; the relics of St Oswald were translated to the new minster at Gloucester.

events.label: Sole rule as Lady of the Mercians after Æthelred's death
events.labelCn: 埃塞尔雷德去世后独揽大权，称麦西亚夫人
events.note: On Æthelred's death in 911 she became Myrcna hlæfdige, 'Lady of the Mercians' — one of the most unique events in early medieval history.

events.label: Fortified Bridgnorth
events.labelCn: 营建布里奇诺斯堡垒
events.note: Part of her programme of building burhs to defend Mercia against the Danes; the site at Bridgnorth was fortified in 912.

events.label: Built burhs at Tamworth and Stafford
events.labelCn: 营建塔姆沃思与斯塔福德堡垒
events.note: Forts at Tamworth and Stafford were constructed in 913; later burhs included Eddisbury, Warwick, Chirbury and Runcorn (914-915).

events.label: Campaign against Brycheiniog; destroyed the Llangorse crannog
events.labelCn: 征讨布雷赫尼奥格，摧毁兰戈尔斯湖上堡垒
events.note: In 916 she sent an army into Brycheiniog which destroyed the royal crannog on Llangorse Lake and captured the queen and 33 companions.

events.label: Captured Derby from the Vikings
events.labelCn: 从维京人手中夺取德比
events.note: She sent an army which captured Derby in 917; the Anglo-Saxon Chronicle gives no month, and July is a later inference.

events.label: Leicester surrendered; York offered submission
events.labelCn: 莱斯特投降；约克表示归顺
events.note: Leicester surrendered without opposition in early 918 and most of its Danish army submitted; the leading men of Danish-ruled York also offered loyalty, but she died before acting on it.

events.label: Died at Tamworth; buried at St Oswald's, Gloucester
events.labelCn: 卒于塔姆沃思，葬于格洛斯特圣奥斯瓦尔德修道院
events.note: Died at Tamworth on 12 June 918; her daughter Ælfwynn briefly succeeded her before Edward the Elder took Mercia under direct rule in December 918.

fullNameCn: 麦西亚夫人埃塞尔弗莱德

primaryTitleCn: 沙夫茨伯里女修道院院长

events.label: Educated at the West Saxon court alongside her brother Edward
events.labelCn: 在威塞克斯宫廷与兄长爱德华一同接受教育
events.note: Ælfthryth was educated together with her brother Edward (later Edward the Elder) — a rare instance of a princess receiving an education equal to a prince's. No exact date is recorded.

events.label: Marriage to Baldwin II, Count of Flanders
events.labelCn: 与佛兰德伯爵鲍德温二世结婚
events.note: Ælfthryth married Baldwin II of Flanders between 893 and 899; their sons were Arnulf (later Count Arnulf I) and Adalolf of Boulogne, and they also had daughters Ealswid and Ermentrud.

events.label: Widowed on the death of Baldwin II
events.labelCn: 鲍德温二世去世，寡居
events.note: Baldwin II died in 918; Ælfthryth survived him by eleven years. Her death is sometimes given as 7 June 929.

events.label: Death; buried at St Peter's Abbey, Ghent
events.labelCn: 去世，葬于根特圣彼得修道院
events.note: Ælfthryth died on 7 June 929, probably in Flanders, and was buried next to her husband at St Peter's Abbey, Ghent.

sourceNote: Daughter of Alfred the Great and wife of Baldwin II of Flanders. Married c. 893–899; died 7 June 929; buried at St Peter's Abbey, Ghent.
notes: Youngest daughter of Alfred the Great and Ealhswith. Married Baldwin II, Count of Flanders (between 893 and 899); mother of Arnulf I of Flanders and Adalolf of Boulogne. IMPORTANT: this Ælfthryth is the Countess of Flanders, who died in 929 — she is NOT the Ælfthryth who married King Edgar (daughter of Ordgar, ealdorman of Devon, died c. 1000–1001). The two are different women, so no spousal link to Edgar is drawn. Her husband Baldwin II and children are not in the roster.

deathCause.summary: Died 7 June 929; buried at St Peter's Abbey, Ghent
deathCause.detail: Ælfthryth died on 7 June 929, probably in Flanders, and was buried next to her husband Baldwin II at St Peter's Abbey, Ghent. The cause of death is not recorded.
deathCause.summaryCn: 929年6月7日去世，葬于根特圣彼得修道院
deathCause.detailCn: 埃尔夫特里特于929年6月7日去世，地点可能在佛兰德；她被安葬于根特圣彼得修道院，与丈夫鲍德温二世相邻。死因未载。

fullNameCn: 法兰西国王路易八世
deathPlaceCn: 法兰西王国的蒙庞西耶
notes: Son of Philippe II Augustus and Isabella of Hainaut. Spouse Blanche of Castile and children (including Louis IX) are not yet in the roster; links to be added when those records exist.

deathCause.detail: Louis VIII died of dysentery on 8 November 1226 at the Château de Montpensier in Auvergne while returning from the Albigensian crusade.
deathCause.detailCn: 1226 年 11 月 8 日，路易八世在阿尔比十字军归途中因痢疾死于奥弗涅的蒙庞西耶城堡。

events.label: Born in Paris
events.labelCn: 出生于巴黎

events.label: Marriage to Blanche of Castile
events.labelCn: 与卡斯蒂利亚的布兰奇成婚
events.note: Blanche was the daughter of Alfonso VIII of Castile and Eleanor of England; the marriage was part of the Le Goulet settlement.

events.label: Crusading campaign in Languedoc
events.labelCn: 朗格多克十字军行动
events.note: At Narbonne and Toulouse in April 1215, fulfilling his father's crusading vow.

events.label: Led the Albigensian Crusade
events.labelCn: 领导阿尔比十字军
events.note: Led royal forces in Languedoc from 1219 to 1223 in support of Simon de Montfort.

events.label: Became King of France
events.labelCn: 成为法兰西国王

events.label: Coronation at Reims
events.labelCn: 兰斯加冕

events.label: Took the cross for the royal crusade
events.labelCn: 为王家十字军立誓

events.label: Capture of Avignon
events.labelCn: 攻占阿维尼翁
events.note: The city surrendered on 9 September 1226 after a three-month siege, agreeing to pay 6,000 marks and raze its walls.

events.label: Died of dysentery at Montpensier
events.labelCn: 蒙庞西耶因痢疾去世
events.note: Died at the Château de Montpensier in Auvergne while returning from the Albigensian crusade.

fullName: Isabella of Hainaut, Queen of France
fullNameCn: 法兰西王后埃诺的伊莎贝尔
notes: First wife of Philippe II Augustus. Parents (Baldwin V of Hainaut and Margaret I of Flanders) are not yet in the roster.

deathCause.detail: Isabella gave birth to twin sons on 14 March 1190 (both died within days) and died the next day, 15 March 1190, aged 19. She was buried in Notre-Dame de Paris.
deathCause.detailCn: 1190 年 3 月 14 日伊莎贝尔产下一对双胞胎儿子（数日内先后夭折），次日（3 月 15 日）去世，年仅 19 岁，葬于巴黎圣母院。

events.label: Born in Valenciennes
events.labelCn: 出生于瓦朗谢讷

events.label: Marriage to Philippe II at Bapaume
events.labelCn: 在巴波姆与腓力二世成婚
events.note: Her dowry was the county of Artois; both bride and groom were fifteen.

events.label: Coronation as Queen of France
events.labelCn: 加冕为法兰西王后
events.note: Crowned at Saint-Denis.

events.label: Birth of Louis VIII
events.labelCn: 路易八世出生

events.label: Birth of twin sons Robert and Philippe
events.labelCn: 诞下双胞胎罗伯特与菲利普
events.note: Robert died the same day and Philippe three days later; both are excluded from the roster as infants who died young.

events.label: Died in Paris following childbirth
events.labelCn: 分娩后在巴黎去世
events.note: Philippe II was away campaigning in Normandy and did not attend the funeral.

fullName: Ingeborg of Denmark, Queen of France
fullNameCn: 法兰西王后丹麦的英格堡
deathPlace: Priory of Saint-Jean-de-l'Île, near Corbeil, Kingdom of France
deathPlaceCn: 法兰西王国科尔贝附近的圣让岛修道院
sourceNote: Birth year uncertain (c. 1174/75); birthplace not recorded. Death date varies across sources (1236–1238; Wikipedia infobox gives 29 July 1237). Parents (Valdemar I of Denmark and Sofia of Minsk) are not yet in the roster.
notes: Second wife of Philippe II Augustus. Married 1193, repudiated the same day; the annulment was never canonically granted, and after the interdict crisis she was restored and remained queen until Philippe's death. The estrangement is modelled in events, not as a former marriage.

deathCause.summary: Died at the Priory of Saint-Jean-de-l'Île
deathCause.detail: Ingeborg died on 29 July 1237 (some sources give 1236 or 1238) at the Priory of Saint-Jean-de-l'Île near Corbeil, and was buried in the church of the Order of St John in Corbeil.
deathCause.detailCn: 1237 年 7 月 29 日（有资料作 1236 或 1238 年），英格堡在科尔贝附近的圣让岛修道院去世，葬于科尔贝圣约翰骑士团教堂。

events.label: Born in Denmark
events.labelCn: 出生于丹麦
events.note: Birth year uncertain (c. 1174/75); birthplace not recorded. Daughter of Valdemar I of Denmark and Sofia of Minsk.

events.label: Marriage to Philippe II
events.labelCn: 与腓力二世成婚
events.note: Married at Amiens on 14 August 1193 (the infobox gives 15 August); Philippe repudiated her the very next day, but the repudiation never obtained canonical validity.

events.label: Coronation as Queen of France
events.labelCn: 加冕为法兰西王后

events.label: Council of Compiègne annulment attempt
events.labelCn: 贡比涅会议企图宣告婚姻无效
events.note: About three months after the wedding Philippe summoned a council at Compiègne to annul the marriage; Danish envoys carried her appeal to Rome.

events.label: Interdict on France over the repudiation
events.labelCn: 法国因休妻事件被施以禁罚
events.note: Innocent III placed France under interdict (sources give 1199 or 1200); it was lifted in September 1200 when Philippe agreed to obey the pope.

events.label: Restored as Queen of France
events.labelCn: 恢复法兰西王后身份

events.label: Full reconciliation with Philippe II
events.labelCn: 与腓力二世完全和解
events.note: Philippe reconciled with Ingeborg in 1213, after Agnes of Meran's death; she remained queen until his death in 1223.

events.label: Died at Saint-Jean-de-l'Île
events.labelCn: 在圣让岛修道院去世
events.note: Died 29 July 1237 (some sources 1236 or 1238) near Corbeil.

fullNameCn: 梅拉尼亚的阿涅丝
sourceNote: Birth year and birthplace uncertain (Wikipedia gives 1175, other sources c. 1180). Parents (Berthold IV of Merania and Agnes of Rochlitz) are not yet in the roster.
notes: Third wife of Philippe II Augustus. The 1196 marriage was contracted while Ingeborg lived and was declared invalid in 1201; her children were legitimised in November 1201. She was treated as queen but never canonically queen consort. Modelled as a former marriage (broken line), following the Eleanor x Louis VII pattern.

deathCause.detail: Agnes died in July 1201 at the castle of Poissy, possibly in childbirth, and was buried in the Convent of Saint-Corentin near Mantes.
deathCause.detailCn: 1201 年 7 月，阿涅丝在普瓦西城堡去世（可能死于分娩），葬于芒特附近的圣科朗坦修道院。

events.label: Born in Merania
events.labelCn: 出生于梅拉尼亚
events.note: Birth year uncertain (c. 1175–1180); birthplace not recorded. Daughter of Berthold IV, Duke of Merania, of the House of Andechs.

events.label: Marriage to Philippe II
events.labelCn: 与腓力二世成婚
events.note: Married June 1196 while Philippe's second wife Ingeborg was still living; under canon law the marriage was never valid.

events.label: Birth of Marie
events.labelCn: 女儿玛丽出生

events.label: Birth of Philippe Hurepel
events.labelCn: 儿子菲利普·于雷佩尔出生

events.label: Died at Poissy
events.labelCn: 在普瓦西去世
events.note: Died in July 1201 (some sources give 19/20 July), possibly in childbirth; her marriage had been declared invalid earlier that year.

events.label: Children legitimised by Pope Innocent III
events.labelCn: 子女获教皇英诺森三世承认为婚生
events.note: Marie and Philippe Hurepel were legitimised by papal dispensation in November 1201, after Agnes's death.

fullName: Marie of France, Duchess of Brabant
fullNameCn: 布拉班特公爵夫人玛丽
sourceNote: Birthplace unrecorded. Death date 15 August 1224 per Wikipedia (some sources 1223). Spouse Henry I of Brabant and children are not yet in the roster.
notes: Daughter of Philippe II Augustus and Agnes of Meran; legitimised with her brother Philippe Hurepel in November 1201.

deathCause.detail: Marie died on 15 August 1224 and was buried at Affligem Abbey (some sources give St Peter's Church, Leuven).
deathCause.detailCn: 玛丽于 1224 年 8 月 15 日去世，葬于阿夫利赫姆修道院（有资料作鲁汶圣彼得教堂）。

events.label: Born to Philippe II and Agnes of Meran
events.labelCn: 腓力二世与阿涅丝之女出生

events.label: Legitimised by Pope Innocent III
events.labelCn: 获教皇英诺森三世承认为婚生
events.note: Legitimised with her brother Philippe Hurepel after their parents' marriage was declared invalid.

events.label: Marriage to Henry I, Duke of Brabant
events.labelCn: 与布拉班特公爵亨利一世成婚
events.note: Married at Soissons on 22 April 1213.

events.label: Died
events.labelCn: 去世
events.note: Buried at Affligem Abbey; some sources give St Peter's Church, Leuven.

fullNameCn: 布洛涅伯爵菲利普·于雷佩尔
sourceNote: Birth September 1200 per Wikipedia. Marriage to Matilda II of Boulogne c. 1223 per Wikipedia (some older sources give 1216). Death year 1235 per Wikipedia (some sources 1234). Spouse and children are not yet in the roster.
notes: Son of Philippe II Augustus and Agnes of Meran; legitimised in November 1201. Count of Boulogne jure uxoris and Count of Clermont.

deathCause.detail: Philippe Hurepel died in 1235 (some sources give 1234); the cause is unrecorded.
deathCause.detailCn: 菲利普·于雷佩尔于 1235 年去世（有资料作 1234 年），死因无记载。

events.label: Born to Philippe II and Agnes of Meran
events.labelCn: 腓力二世与阿涅丝之子出生

events.label: Legitimised by Pope Innocent III
events.labelCn: 获教皇英诺森三世承认为婚生
events.note: Legitimised with his sister Marie after their parents' marriage was declared invalid.

events.label: Marriage to Matilda II, Countess of Boulogne
events.labelCn: 与布洛涅女伯爵玛蒂尔达二世成婚
events.note: Married c. 1223; through her he held Boulogne, Mortain, Aumale and Dammartin jure uxoris.

events.label: Became Count of Boulogne jure uxoris
events.labelCn: 以妻权成为布洛涅伯爵

events.label: Revolt against Blanche of Castile
events.labelCn: 起兵反抗卡斯蒂利亚的布兰奇
events.note: Joined the baronial league opposing the regent Blanche after Louis VIII's death in 1226.

events.label: Died
events.labelCn: 去世
events.note: Died 1235 (some sources 1234) at Corbie; cause unrecorded.

fullNameCn: 努瓦永主教皮埃尔·夏洛
deathPlace: Near Cyprus, returning from the Seventh Crusade
deathPlaceCn: 第七次十字军归途中塞浦路斯附近
sourceNote: Birth year uncertain (between 1205 and 1209); mother unnamed (a lady of Arras). Illegitimate son of Philippe II Augustus.
notes: Illegitimate son of Philippe II Augustus; Treasurer of Saint-Martin of Tours and Bishop of Noyon. Died near Cyprus returning from the Seventh Crusade.

deathCause.detail: Pierre Charlot died in 1249 near Cyprus while returning from the Seventh Crusade with Louis IX, and was buried in the cathedral of Noyon.
deathCause.detailCn: 1249 年，皮埃尔·夏洛随路易九世参加第七次十字军，在归途中于塞浦路斯附近去世，葬于努瓦永大教堂。

events.label: Born as an illegitimate son of Philippe II
events.labelCn: 作为腓力二世的私生子出生
events.note: Born between 1205 and 1209; his mother is unnamed in the sources (a lady of Arras).

events.label: Became Treasurer of Saint-Martin of Tours
events.labelCn: 出任图尔圣马丁教堂司库
events.note: Appointed by 1232.

events.label: Elected Bishop of Noyon
events.labelCn: 当选努瓦永主教
events.note: A tied election was decided in Rome in his favour.

events.label: Died near Cyprus on the return from the Seventh Crusade
events.labelCn: 第七次十字军归途中在塞浦路斯附近去世
events.note: Died in 1249 near Cyprus; buried in the cathedral of Noyon.

fullNameCn: 法兰西国王路易九世
notes: Son of Louis VIII and Blanche of Castile (Blanche is not yet in the roster; the mother link will be added when her record exists). Spouse Margaret of Provence and children other than Philippe III are not yet in the roster. Canonised in 1297 — the only French king to be made a saint.

deathCause.detail: Louis IX died on 25 August 1270 at Tunis of dysentery (some sources suggest plague or typhus) during the Eighth Crusade.
deathCause.detailCn: 1270 年 8 月 25 日，路易九世在第八次十字军东征期间于突尼斯因痢疾（有资料作瘟疫或伤寒）去世。

events.label: Born at Poissy
events.labelCn: 出生于普瓦西

events.label: Became King of France at age twelve
events.labelCn: 十二岁即位为法兰西国王
events.note: His mother Blanche of Castile ruled as regent during his minority.

events.label: Coronation at Reims
events.labelCn: 兰斯加冕

events.label: Marriage to Margaret of Provence
events.labelCn: 与普罗旺斯的玛格丽特成婚
events.note: Margaret is not yet in the roster.

events.label: Consecration of the Sainte-Chapelle
events.labelCn: 圣礼拜堂祝圣
events.note: Built to house the relics of the Passion, including the Crown of Thorns.

events.label: Seventh Crusade: capture of Damietta
events.labelCn: 第七次十字军：攻占杜姆亚特

events.label: Battle of Mansurah and capture
events.labelCn: 曼苏拉之战与被俘
events.note: Defeated and captured in April 1250; ransomed in May 1250.

events.label: Treaty of Paris with Henry III
events.labelCn: 与亨利三世缔结《巴黎条约》
events.note: Henry III renounced claims to Normandy, Anjou and Poitou while Louis conceded parts of Aquitaine.

events.label: Eighth Crusade against Tunis
events.labelCn: 第八次十字军远征突尼斯

events.label: Died at Tunis
events.labelCn: 在突尼斯去世

events.label: Canonised as Saint Louis
events.labelCn: 被封圣为圣路易
events.note: Canonised by Pope Boniface VIII; the only canonised king of France.

fullNameCn: 法兰西国王腓力三世
notes: Son of Louis IX and Margaret of Provence (Margaret is not yet in the roster). Spouses Isabella of Aragon and Marie of Brabant, and children other than Philippe IV, are not yet in the roster.

deathCause.detail: Philippe III died on 5 October 1285 at Perpignan of dysentery while retreating from the Aragonese Crusade.
deathCause.detailCn: 1285 年 10 月 5 日，腓力三世在阿拉贡十字军撤退途中于佩皮尼昂因痢疾去世。

events.label: Born at Poissy
events.labelCn: 出生于普瓦西

events.label: Marriage to Isabella of Aragon
events.labelCn: 与阿拉贡的伊莎贝拉成婚
events.note: Isabella is not yet in the roster.

events.label: Became King of France
events.labelCn: 即位为法兰西国王
events.note: Succeeded while on the Eighth Crusade with his father.

events.label: Coronation at Reims
events.labelCn: 兰斯加冕

events.label: Sicilian Vespers and the fall of Charles of Anjou's Sicily
events.labelCn: 西西里晚祷与安茹查理失去西西里
events.note: The revolt against his uncle Charles of Anjou drew Philippe into the Aragonese conflict.

events.label: Aragonese Crusade and retreat
events.labelCn: 阿拉贡十字军与败退
events.note: The expedition against Peter III of Aragon collapsed amid epidemic; Philippe died on the retreat.

events.label: Died at Perpignan
events.labelCn: 在佩皮尼昂去世

fullNameCn: 法兰西国王腓力四世
sourceNote: Birth in April–June 1268 (exact day unrecorded).
notes: Son of Philippe III and Isabella of Aragon. Spouse Joan I of Navarre (through whom he held Navarre) and daughter Isabella of France are not yet in the roster.

deathCause.summary: Died of a stroke at Fontainebleau
deathCause.detail: Philippe IV died on 29 November 1314 at Fontainebleau, several weeks after a cerebral stroke suffered during a hunt (popularly linked to the Templar grand master's alleged curse).
deathCause.detailCn: 1314 年 11 月 29 日，腓力四世在枫丹白露去世；数周前他在狩猎时中风（民间传说将之与圣殿骑士团大团长的诅咒相联系）。

events.label: Born at Fontainebleau
events.labelCn: 出生于枫丹白露
events.note: Born April–June 1268; exact day unrecorded.

events.label: Marriage to Joan I of Navarre
events.labelCn: 与纳瓦拉的让娜一世成婚
events.note: Through Joan he became King of Navarre jure uxoris; Joan is not yet in the roster.

events.label: Became King of France
events.labelCn: 即位为法兰西国王

events.label: Coronation at Reims
events.labelCn: 兰斯加冕

events.label: First Estates-General convened
events.labelCn: 召开第一次三级会议
events.note: Summoned to rally support in the conflict with Pope Boniface VIII.

events.label: Conflict with Boniface VIII: Unam Sanctam
events.labelCn: 与卜尼法斯八世的冲突：〈一圣教谕〉

events.label: Outrage of Anagni
events.labelCn: 阿纳尼事件
events.note: Boniface VIII was seized at Anagni by Guillaume de Nogaret's force; he died weeks later.

events.label: Arrest of the Knights Templar
events.labelCn: 逮捕圣殿骑士团
events.note: Mass arrests across France; the order was suppressed at the Council of Vienne in 1312 and its grand master Jacques de Molay burned in March 1314.

events.label: Papacy moved to Avignon
events.labelCn: 教廷迁至阿维尼翁
events.note: Clement V, a French pope under Philippe's influence, settled the curia at Avignon.

events.label: Died at Fontainebleau
events.labelCn: 在枫丹白露去世

fullNameCn: 法兰西国王路易十世
notes: Eldest son of Philippe IV and Joan I of Navarre. Spouses Margaret of Burgundy and Clementia of Hungary, and daughter Joan II of Navarre, are not yet in the roster.

deathCause.detail: Louis X died on 5 June 1316 at Vincennes, probably of pleurisy or pneumonia after a game of tennis; poisoning rumours circulated at the time.
deathCause.detailCn: 1316 年 6 月 5 日，路易十世在万塞讷去世，可能是网球运动后患上胸膜炎或肺炎；当时曾有下毒传言。

events.label: Born in Paris
events.labelCn: 出生于巴黎

events.label: Marriage to Margaret of Burgundy
events.labelCn: 与勃艮第的玛格丽特成婚
events.note: Margaret is not yet in the roster.

events.label: Tour de Nesle affair
events.labelCn: 奈斯勒塔丑闻
events.note: Margaret of Burgundy was convicted of adultery and imprisoned; her death in 1315 (officially of illness) cleared the way for Louis's remarriage.

events.label: Became King of France
events.labelCn: 即位为法兰西国王

events.label: Marriage to Clementia of Hungary
events.labelCn: 与匈牙利的克莱门西娅成婚
events.note: Clementia is not yet in the roster; their posthumous son became John I.

events.label: Coronation at Reims
events.labelCn: 兰斯加冕

events.label: Died at Vincennes
events.labelCn: 在万塞讷去世
events.note: His pregnant widow gave birth to John I in November 1316, triggering the succession crisis.

fullNameCn: 法兰西国王约翰一世
sourceNote: Mother Clementia of Hungary is not yet in the roster. Alternate dates (13–18 November) appear in the Chronique Parisienne Anonyme.
notes: Posthumous son of Louis X; the only French king to reign for his entire life (15–19 November 1316, four/five days). His death broke three centuries of father-to-son succession and opened the dispute that led Philippe V to exclude women from the succession. A 14th-century impostor (Giannino Baglioni) later claimed to be him.

deathCause.detail: John I died on 19 November 1316, four or five days after his birth; the cause is unknown and rumours of poisoning circulated immediately.
deathCause.detailCn: 1316 年 11 月 19 日，约翰一世在出生四五天后夭折；死因不明，当时即有下毒传言。

events.label: Born as posthumous son of Louis X
events.labelCn: 作为路易十世的遗腹子出生
events.note: His uncle Philippe, Count of Poitiers, acted as regent.

events.label: Proclaimed King of France at birth
events.labelCn: 出生即被宣布为法兰西国王
events.note: The only king of France to hold the title for his entire life.

events.label: Died five days after birth
events.labelCn: 出生五日后夭折
events.note: His death ended three centuries of father-to-son succession and triggered the exclusion of women from the French succession.

fullNameCn: 法兰西国王腓力五世
deathPlace: Abbey of Longchamp, Paris, Kingdom of France
deathPlaceCn: 法兰西王国巴黎隆尚修道院
sourceNote: Birth year c. 1291 (some sources 1293/94).
notes: Second son of Philippe IV. Spouse Joan II, Countess of Burgundy, is not yet in the roster (their Navarrese claim passed to their daughters). Left no male heir; his infant son Philippe (1316–1317) died young.

deathCause.detail: Philippe V died on 3 January 1322 at the Abbey of Longchamp near Paris, aged about 30, of dysentery (the sources also speak of multiple illnesses).
deathCause.detailCn: 1322 年 1 月 3 日，腓力五世在巴黎附近的隆尚修道院去世，年仅约 30 岁，死于痢疾（史料亦提及多种疾病）。

events.label: Born in Lyon
events.labelCn: 出生于里昂
events.note: Born c. 1291; some sources give 1293/94.

events.label: Marriage to Joan II, Countess of Burgundy
events.labelCn: 与勃艮第女伯爵让娜二世成婚
events.note: Joan is not yet in the roster.

events.label: Regent for the unborn heir
events.labelCn: 出任待产王储的摄政
events.note: After Louis X's death he governed as regent pending the birth of John I.

events.label: Became King of France
events.labelCn: 即位为法兰西国王
events.note: Succeeded his infant nephew John I over the claim of John's half-sister Joan.

events.label: Coronation at Reims
events.labelCn: 兰斯加冕

events.label: Assembly established the exclusion of women from the succession
events.labelCn: 议会确立女性排除于王位继承之外
events.note: The Paris assembly of 2 February 1317 asserted the principle later known as the Salic law, consolidating his own title.

events.label: Shepherds' Crusade
events.labelCn: 牧人十字军
events.note: A popular movement that turned to attacks on Jews and clergy and was suppressed during his reign.

events.label: Died at Longchamp
events.labelCn: 在隆尚修道院去世

fullNameCn: 法兰西国王查理四世
sourceNote: Born 18/19 June 1294 (day varies across sources).
notes: Third son of Philippe IV; the last king of the direct Capetian line. His death without a male heir (only daughters survived) opened the succession dispute between Philippe of Valois and Edward III of England, a proximate cause of the Hundred Years' War. Spouses (Blanche of Burgundy, Marie of Luxembourg, Jeanne d'Évreux) are not yet in the roster.

deathCause.detail: Charles IV died on 1 February 1328 at Vincennes after a prolonged illness (various sources mention gout, tuberculosis or consumption).
deathCause.detailCn: 1328 年 2 月 1 日，查理四世在久病后于万塞讷去世（资料提及痛风、结核或痨病）。

events.label: Born at Clermont
events.labelCn: 出生于克莱蒙
events.note: Born 18/19 June 1294; the day varies across sources.

events.label: Became King of France
events.labelCn: 即位为法兰西国王

events.label: Coronation at Reims
events.labelCn: 兰斯加冕

events.label: Marriage to Blanche of Burgundy annulled
events.labelCn: 与勃艮第的布朗什的婚姻被宣告无效
events.note: Blanche had been imprisoned for adultery after the Tour de Nesle affair; the annulment (19 May 1322) permitted Charles's remarriage.

events.label: Marriage to Marie of Luxembourg
events.labelCn: 与卢森堡的玛丽成婚
events.note: Marie is not yet in the roster.

events.label: War of Saint-Sardos with England
events.labelCn: 与英格兰的圣萨尔多战争
events.note: The Gascon conflict of 1323–1328 ended with the confiscation of most English-held Aquitaine.

events.label: Died without a male heir
events.labelCn: 去世，无男性继承人
events.note: His death ended the direct Capetian line; the rival claims of Philippe of Valois and Edward III of England led to the Hundred Years' War.
